title: Specify needs
description: This phase is triggered when a need for new statistics is identified, perhaps resulting from user feedback, or a review is undertaken. It includes all activities associated with engaging stakeholders to identify their detailed statistical needs (current or future), proposing high level solution options and preparing a business case, which may weigh the benefits of addressing these needs against expected costs, risks and other requirements, considering the public good arising from meeting those needs and the implications for respondents, users and other stakeholders. The Specify Needs phase is broken down into six sub-processes (Figure 7), which are presented sequentially, from left to right, but can also occur in parallel, and can be iterative.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: Evaluating, recommending, and leading studies related to strategic objectives, anticipating and understanding needs for new data, assessing impact, and revising programs all align with the phase’s requirements for needs identification, user engagement, high-level solution options, and stakeholder analysis. The 'Senior Analyst, Socio-Economic Analysis' role encompasses: 'Leads research to assess current and future requirements for statistical data; conducts analyses... and provides advice and recommendations concerning changes or improvements to policies, strategic plans, programs, and services.'
implicated work-descriptions.title: Senior Analyst, Socio-Economic Analysis

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This role's activities in consulting with evaluation managers, program managers, and stakeholders, coordinating studies/projects involving cross-departmental collaboration, estimating resources, managing the design of data collection tools, and developing evaluation reports all support identifying needs, resource/cost implications, and preparing business cases. Responsibilities include: 'Consults with Evaluation Manager and program managers... recommends project objectives, scope, approaches... negotiates and secures agreement on activities,' as well as 'initiates and coordinates complex studies involving other government departments, partners and stakeholders.'
implicated work-descriptions.title: Manager, Evaluation and Strategic Planning

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The 'Evaluation Analyst' role directly engages in determining and analyzing current and future requirements for statistical data, literature and data research, synthesizing and interpreting information, and drafting recommendations. These support needs identification and feed into business case development: 'Assesses current and future requirements for statistical data; interprets and analyzes statistical information... to support findings and conclusions concerning various elements of evaluations.'
implicated work-descriptions.title: Evaluation Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The 'Evaluation Officer' role supports phase 1 by conducting literature and data research, participating in interviews, analyzing requirements, and contributing to reports for management regarding programs, data needs, and evaluation results: 'Assesses current requirements for data; interprets and analyzes information and databases to support findings and conclusions concerning various elements of evaluations.' This basis is central for defining and justifying statistical needs.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Evaluation Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This role is responsible for reviewing the relevancy of collection/processing methods, determining needed changes, and interpreting user needs for statistical information—which links directly to determining what statistics are needed, the options for provision, data source suitability, and potential business process modification. Example: 'Interprets program and user needs for statistical information, assesses the suitability of existing data products and services and translates them into a concrete, timely and affordable product.'
implicated work-descriptions.title: Section Chief, Statistical Program Development

title: Identify needs
description: This sub-process includes the initial investigation and identification of what statistics are needed and what is needed of the statistics. It may be triggered by a new information request from users, an environmental change such as a reduced budget, a periodic review, or respondent feedback. Action plans from evaluations of previous iterations of the production cycle (including from respondent feedback) or from other programmes might provide an input to this sub-process. It also includes consideration of practice amongst other (national and international) statistical organisations producing similar data and the methods used by those organisations.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This role encompasses analysis and interpretation of requests for statistical information and translation into concrete, timely, and affordable information requests. It also includes conducting research and comparative analysis on statistical products of different national statistical offices to recommend improvements, and synthesizing broad environmental context and subject-matter needs. This directly supports the identification of information/statistics needs, environmental scanning, review of practices in other organisations, and response to new information requests. See key tasks: 'Analysis is required to understand and interpret requests for statistical information and to translate them into a concrete, timely and affordable information request.' 'Conducts research and comparative analysis on statistical products of different national statistical offices...' and 'Knowledge of current and emerging socio-economic issues in Canada and internationally... to analyze program outputs, anticipate and understand needs for new data, and assess the impact on the area of specialization.'
implicated work-descriptions.title: Senior Analyst, Socio-Economic Analysis

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This position is responsible for leading research and comparative analysis on the statistical products and methods used by national and international statistical offices, and for proposing improvements based on identified gaps or overlaps. This supports identifying best practices and approaches of other statistical organizations as required in this sub-process: 'Conducts research and comparative analysis on statistical products of different national statistical offices in order to recommend areas of improvement.'
implicated work-descriptions.title: Senior Advisor, International Cooperation

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This role leads and participates in periodic reviews, evaluates new information requests and respondent feedback, and integrates findings into needs identification. It provides specialized knowledge necessary for initial investigation of required information and ongoing assessment of information gaps: 'Knowledge of economic/sociologic principles and practices as they relate to a specialized area... to initiate and conduct projects to improve existing concepts in other countries or develop new approaches to extend the application of official statistics internationally.' and 'Skill in synthesizing information from diverse disciplines... to propose solutions that are feasible, reflect current best practices, and are multifaceted, addressing several challenges simultaneously.'
implicated work-descriptions.title: Senior Advisor, International Cooperation

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This role identifies user data requirements, interprets program and user needs for information, and reviews and determines the suitability, relevance, and gaps of current products/services. The activities here are essential in the process of investigating what statistics are needed, conducting ongoing periodic reviews, and evaluating changes required by environmental shifts: 'Interprets user requests to determine the nature, feasibility, and options for providing the information required.' and 'Analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems.'
implicated work-descriptions.title: Section Chief, Statistical Program Development

implicated work-descriptions.justification: Supports project teams by gathering, synthesizing, and analyzing user requirements and environmental information from internal and external sources; participates in focus groups, interviews, and literature/data research to provide evidence for identifying new or evolving needs and assessing recent changes. Example: 'Assesses current requirements for data; interprets and analyzes information and databases to support findings and conclusions concerning various elements of Statistics Canada evaluations.' and 'Participates... in the conduct of evaluation studies related to Statistics Canada programs, policies and initiatives, to evaluate their relevance and performance.'
implicated work-descriptions.title: Evaluation Officer

title: Consult and confirm needs
description: This sub-process focuses on consulting with the internal and external stakeholders and confirming in detail the needs for the statistics. A good understanding of user needs is required so that the statistical organisation knows not only what it is expected to deliver, but also when, how, and perhaps most importantly, why. For the second and subsequent iterations of this sub-process, the main focus will be on determining whether previously identified needs have changed. This detailed understanding of user needs is the critical part of this sub-process.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This role is responsible for consulting and negotiating with program managers, stakeholders, and representatives from other departments to confirm evaluation project objectives, requirements, and resources. Key activities include: 'Consults with the Evaluation Manager and Statistics Canada program managers, in order to discuss and recommend project objectives, scope, approaches to be utilized, the timing and resources required for studies and projects and negotiates and secures agreement on courses of action and activities to be taken.' These tasks map directly to the consultative confirmation of statistical needs and requirements described in the sub-process.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Manager, Evaluation and Strategic Planning

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This role requires stakeholder engagement through participation and leadership in working groups, interdepartmental, and intergovernmental committees, as well as consulting to develop consensus and ensure consultation on policies, plans, and statistical products. The description states: 'Participates in, and leads, working groups, task forces and committees as an expert in the development, production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata in various roles such as Project Manager, Task Manager or Senior Advisor.' and 'Liaises with other statistical metadata specialists, systems specialists, clients and managers to plan statistical metadata projects...' Such direct stakeholder engagement is central to confirming statistical needs.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Unit Head, Metadata Development, Dissemination and Evaluation

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The core of this role is extensive consultation and advisory activity with a broad array of internal and external users (e.g., academics, policy makers, international bodies), providing expert advice based on analytical studies and survey concepts, and representing various stakeholders in the presentation and refinement of statistical content: 'Provides expert advisory and consultative services to data users (e.g. academics, policy makers, international bodies, etc.) and other professionals on the results of research and analytical studies, economic / social science theories and principles and advanced survey concepts and methods.' and 'Represents departmental interests when presenting analytical research and modelling studies to a variety of stakeholders.'
implicated work-descriptions.title: Senior Advisor, Socio-Economic Analysis

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This role is deeply involved in ongoing consultation and collaboration, including: 'Attends Departmental, interdepartmental and stakeholder meetings to discuss data/information requirements, trends, gaps in information, problems, results, opportunities and effects on new or revised policies and programs.' Establishing and expanding client/stakeholder networks is fundamental to confirming user needs and ensuring the statistical organization's outputs are aligned with them.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Senior Data Analyst / Scientist

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Evaluation Officer contributes to stakeholder engagement by participating in project teams, organizing and attending meetings, and conducting interviews and focus groups with data users and other internal/external stakeholders: 'Participates as a member of project teams, in the conduct of evaluation studies related to Statistics Canada programs, policies and initiatives...' and 'Attends departmental and inter-departmental meetings, when required, to discuss files, issues and evaluation requirements; interprets and reports on trends...'. These activities enable a detailed and iterative confirmation and documentation of user needs.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Evaluation Officer

title: Establish output objectives
description: This sub-process identifies the statistical output objectives that are required to meet the user needs confirmed in sub-process 1.2 (Consult and confirm needs). It includes agreeing the suitability of the proposed outputs and their quality measures with users. Legal or normative frameworks (e.g. relating to confidentiality, methodologies), and available resources are important to consider when establishing output objectives.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This role’s responsibilities include analyzing and determining statistical objectives and outputs, reviewing collection and processing methods for output relevancy, considering legal (Statistics and Privacy Acts) and quality requirements, and advising on subject-matter concepts and output requirements. Relevant evidence: 'Reviews current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems.' and 'Assesses and determines the impact and the constraints on results of the different concepts, definitions and conditions under which the data was collected, processed and stored.' This directly supports defining output objectives, quality measures, and their suitability and feasibility within legal and operational frameworks.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Section Chief, Statistical Program Development

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This role coordinates and organizes the validation, marketing, and dissemination of data, participates in subject-area working groups, and provides subject matter advice/direction to users on output requirements and definitions. Evidence: 'Provides subject matter advice and direction to users on matters relating to subject-matter concepts used in the development and operation of a statistical database...' and 'Participates as a subject area representative on various teams and working groups.' These activities support stakeholder agreement on output objectives and requirements, as well as the translation of user needs into output specifications.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator

implicated work-descriptions.justification: Responsible for developing, maintaining, and supporting statistical production and dissemination processes/outputs, coordinating divisional and external partners, and offering consultative expertise regarding production systems for ongoing statistical program delivery. Evidence: 'Coordinates activities of multiple Statistic Canada divisional partners and other external partners to process, validate, and disseminate statistical data.' and 'Integrates input from multiple economic subject matter areas to develop and maintain complex systems and frameworks for the ongoing production, validation and dissemination of a range of specialized, high-impact statistical outputs.' These support the establishment, agreement, and operationalization of output objectives and quality across program areas.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Production and Database Expert

implicated work-descriptions.justification: Provides specialized statistical, advisory, and consultative services, develops recommendations, advises management, and implements initiatives responding to user needs for high-quality statistical outputs (including the understanding of divisional mandate, legal frameworks, and output quality measures). Evidence: 'Develops recommendations, provides advice to management and implements initiatives pertaining to new methods of acquiring, processing, modeling, analyzing or disseminating data to meet user needs.' and 'Knowledge of divisional and organizational mandate, activities, priorities and practices applicable to the work.' This supports translating user needs into output specifications and quality agreements.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Analytics and Integration Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: Participates in planning and conducting analysis of statistical production; knowledge of system analysis, output validation, relevant legal acts, and assessment of outputs and constraints as required for setting output objectives and standards. Evidence: 'Knowledge of system analysis and design... to design, develop, test, maintain and implement processing systems; to design specifications for the testing of data, and to maintain and use databases.' and 'Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts... and of Statistics Canada policies to ensure understanding and application in the collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of data.'
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer

title: Identify concepts
description: This sub-process clarifies the required concepts to be measured from the point of view of the users. At this stage, the concepts identified might not align with existing statistical standards. This alignment, and the choice or definition of the statistical and other concepts and variables to be used, takes place in sub-process 2.2 (Design variables).

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This role liaises with specialists and users to translate subject-matter requirements into system specifications, communicates detailed subject matter and technical concepts, definitions, and provides advice to users on subject-matter concepts for statistical databases. These activities directly support clarifying required concepts and definitions to be measured from the user's perspective and developing the conceptual basis for statistical products. For example: 'Provides advice to data users and clients on matters relating to subject-matter concepts used in the development and operation of a statistical database and to the data processing environment in general.' and 'Writes and presents detailed subject matter and technical concepts, definitions and terms in common terminology in order to explain and clarify divisional systems and applications.'1
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This role involves analyzing, reviewing, and determining the impact of different concepts, definitions and collection conditions, translating and adapting data to new definitions/concepts, and advising on subject-matter concept and definition issues. This is directly implicated in clarifying and specifying the concepts required to be measured in statistical programs, and noting where user needs may not align with standard frameworks. Evidence includes: 'Analyzes and synthesizes geographic, demographic, social, economic and/or labour market characteristics and prepares profiles and forecasts. Reviews the development of new subject-matter methods, concepts and definitions and conducts studies and analytical projects to improve existing surveys and data.' and 'Analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to determine the need for modification or replacement with alternative systems, methods and procedures.'2
implicated work-descriptions.title: Section Chief, Statistical Program Development

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The responsibilities of this role include providing advice to data users on subject-matter concepts, assisting in the development of conceptual frameworks, integrating conceptually different data from multiple programs, clarifying and analyzing user needs for statistical information and translating those into definitions or variables. Key evidence: 'Provides subject matter advice and direction to users on matters relating to subject-matter concepts used in the development and operation of a statistical database.' and 'Knowledge of current or emerging economic and social issues relating to the program area in order to identify subject-matter concept and definition requirements, and to conduct studies.'3
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Analytics and Integration Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This senior analysis and advisory role involves reviewing the conceptual frameworks of statistical programs, determining the need for new or adapted methods, and integrating data that may have been collected under different concepts or definitions—directly supporting the clarification of user-required concepts even where they do not yet align with standards. Example: 'Reviews the conceptual framework of existing statistical programs and determines the need for development, modification and adaption. Programs involve a combination of statistical techniques and methods and the integration of data from a variety of sources (e.g. financial statements, tax files, other administrative sources, surveys, censuses).'4
implicated work-descriptions.title: Senior Analyst, Socio-Economic Analysis

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This role is responsible for clarifying, explaining, and defending statistical methods and conceptual choices with a wide audience, providing guidance on concepts, and participating in knowledge-sharing and consensus-building meetings—integral to both subject-matter clarification and ensuring shared understanding of required concepts. Example: 'Provides guidance on survey results, methods of socio-economic analysis and statistical techniques and systems.' and 'Chairs intra-departmental meetings and participates in inter-departmental meetings, conferences and groups to develop understanding, consensus and share knowledge of the program area.'5
implicated work-descriptions.title: Senior Advisor, Socio-Economic Analysis

title: Check data availability and suitability
description: This sub-process checks whether current sources of data could meet user requirements and the conditions under which they would be available, including any restrictions on their use. An assessment of possible alternatives would normally include research into potential administrative or other non-statistical sources of data (e.g. privately-held data or “Big Data”), to: Determine whether they would be suitable for use for statistical purposes (e.g. the extent to which administrative concepts match data requirements, and whether the timeliness and quality of the data, security, and continuity of data supply are suitable); Assess the division of responsibilities between data suppliers and the statistical organisation; Check necessary ICT resources (e.g. data storage, technology required to handle incoming data and data processing) as well as any provision agreements with data suppliers (which could be legal or other agreements such as memoranda of understanding) for accessing and sharing the data (e.g. formats, delivery, accompanying metadata and quality check). When existing sources have been assessed, a strategy for filling any remaining gaps in the data requirement is prepared. This may include identifying possible partnerships with data holders or conducting a new survey to collect data if necessary. This sub-process also includes a more general assessment of the legal framework in which data would be collected and used, and may therefore identify proposals for changes to existing legislation or the introduction of a new legal framework.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The role of Senior Analyst, Socio-Economic Analysis is directly implicated because it involves knowledge of data sources, legal (Statistics and Privacy Acts), evaluation of the suitability/quality/security/confidentiality of data, and consultation with data suppliers. Relevant content includes: 'Knowledge of data suppliers to discuss data reporting agreements. Knowledge of data users from governments and from the private sector to identify potential new markets, to understand client needs for complex statistical data or studies, to negotiate contracts and to provide advice on program results.' and 'Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts... and of Statistics Canada policies to explain legislative and policy requirements to other departments, agencies, industry, members of the public and the media. Knowledge of the Statitstics and Privacy Acts is particulary important with respect to the security and confidentiality of information and data provided and to ensure that they and their subordinates do not release any information which may identify an individual or group without prior consent.' Also: 'Reviews and resolves gaps and inconsistencies in the collection methods and procedures... reviews the conceptual framework used and the compatibility with other statistical programs, reviews and resolves technical and conceptual problems referred by staff or project teams.'1
implicated work-descriptions.title: Senior Analyst, Socio-Economic Analysis

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This role leads the assessment and review of data sources, analyzes the suitability, relevancy, and legal/technical constraints of data, assesses the impact of new or modified sources or methods, and participates in data provision agreements and partnerships. Key content: 'Analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems.' and 'Assesses and determines the impact and the constraints on results of the different concepts, definitions and conditions under which the data was collected, processed and stored.' and 'Liaises with other specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development and to suggest improvements to ongoing programs.'2
implicated work-descriptions.title: Section Chief, Statistical Program Development

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The role of Data Analytics and Integration Officer includes reviewing existing and potential data sources, assessing the feasibility and impact of new data acquisition strategies (including legal and security considerations), and recommending solutions for data gaps or partnerships: 'Reviews data collections and information sources to determine the usefulness of existing sources, to propose changes to the data collection approach and to assess the feasibility and impact of new or modified methodologies...' and 'Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts... and of Statistics Canada policies to explain legislative and policy requirements to data suppliers, users and others with respect to the manipulation, storage and retrieval of data.'3
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Analytics and Integration Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This position consolidates and analyzes information/data from multiple sources, supports senior analysts in reviewing and organizing data, and assists in preparing recommendations for data suitability and gap-filling strategies. 'Judgement is required to conduct non-routine data research, assess the relevance and reliability of the data sources and to organize and consolidate findings.' and 'Conducts research and collects data from a variety of sources, aggregating it so that it provides valid and reliable data on which to perform quantitative, retrospective and predictive analysis that measures the impact of the Department’s programs...'4
implicated work-descriptions.title: Junior Data Analyst / Scientist

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Senior Evaluation Analyst role is implicated as it involves the assessment of the relevance, quality, and constraints of program data, including suitability, access issues, legal framework, and recommendations for improved data sourcing and use. Examples: 'Leads research to assess current and future requirements for statistical data...' and 'Initiates and coordinates complex studies and projects involving own and other government departments, partners and stakeholders; identifies project activities and study techniques to be applied...' 'Reviews and resolves gaps and inconsistencies in the collection methods and procedures, reviews the conceptual framework used and the compatibility with other statistical programs, reviews and resolves technical and conceptual problems referred by staff or project teams.'5
implicated work-descriptions.title: Senior Evaluation Analyst

title: Prepare and submit business case
description: This sub-process documents the findings of the other sub-processes in this phase, in the form of a business case to get approval to implement the new or modified statistical business process. Such a business case would need to conform to the requirements of the approval body, but would typically include elements such as: A description of the “As-Is” business process (if it already exists), with information on how the current statistics are produced, highlighting any inefficiencies and issues to be addressed; The proposed “To-Be” solution, detailing how the statistical business process will be developed to produce the new or revised statistics; An assessment of costs and benefits against objectives and any external constraints. The business case describes options and makes recommendations. It may include the benefits, costs, deliverables, time frame, budget, required technical and human resources, risk assessment and impact on stakeholders for each option. After the business case is prepared, it is submitted for approval to move to the next phase of the business process. At this sub-process, a “go”/“no go” decision is made. Typically, the business case is reviewed and formally approved or disapproved by the appropriate sponsors and governance committees.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This role leads, plans and coordinates evaluation studies and research projects, compiles and analyzes data from multiple sources, develops and recommends projections, strategies, and options for program effectiveness, and prepares reports used for decision-making and approval of new or modified processes. Key activities include: 'Develops and recommends strategies to assist departmental managers to effectively integrate program evaluation methodologies into the design and implementation of programs, policies, and initiatives.' and 'Prepares reports on business requirements along with recommendations on alternative solutions to meet those requirements and provides assistance in the design of appropriate business and financial planning processes, strategies and plans to support the integration of strategic business needs.' These functions map directly onto the factual, analytical and recommendation elements of business case construction required by this sub-process. 1
implicated work-descriptions.title: Manager, Planning, Evaluation and Resource Management

implicated work-descriptions.justification: Responsible for planning the development of new or modified statistical and survey methodology (including cost/benefit analysis, operational constraints, and risk assessment), preparing feasibility/planning reports for new survey processes, preparing resource plans, and presenting options and recommendations for process improvement. Key responsibilities: 'Prepares feasibility/planning reports, including cost estimates, for methodology input to new or modified information systems proposed by program managers.' and 'Research on new methods and techniques of data collection, processing and analysis to identify potential benefits in terms of cost, timeliness and quality for existing or new surveys or survey infrastructure.' and 'Prepares comprehensive reports detailing proposed procedures and methodologies (with attendant implementation and maintenance resource implications) for steering committees, external advisory committees and other departments to be used to assess survey or survey support programs and to make recommendations concerning redesign or new development.' These reflect all analytical, planning and proposal elements needed for the business case. 2
implicated work-descriptions.title: Section Chief, Methodology

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This role leads evaluation, prepares assessments, and makes recommendations concerning changes or improvements to agency policies, plans, programs, and services; analyzes costs/benefits, effectiveness, and risks to support business cases for innovation in statistical processes. Task evidence: 'Drafts and writes reports, presentations, briefing notes and memoranda for senior evaluation staff and management on elements of program evaluation related to the various Statistics Canada programs.' and 'Researches, identifies and selects information for evaluations from a variety of sources; analyzes information related to Statistics Canada business lines, policy, program performance, program relevance, success and cost-effectiveness.' This directly underpins business case drafting and approval. 3
implicated work-descriptions.title: Evaluation Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: Compiles, analyzes and synthesizes complex data, prepares knowledge products and presentations to support business case decision-making, tracks and monitors project/system performance, and formulates recommendations for improvements. Example: 'Prepares a variety of knowledge products to present empirical findings of data analytics projects such as reports, dashboards, presentations, speaking points, technical documents or briefing material to guide and support departmental and government direction in data strategy and information requirements.' These materials are core for communicating the rationale for the 'To-be' solution, feasibility, and strategic alignment with goals to an approving committee. 4
implicated work-descriptions.title: Senior Data Scientist/Analyst

title: Design
description: This phase describes the development and design activities, and any associated practical research work needed to define the statistical outputs, variables, methodologies, collection instruments and operational processes, with due regard to other requirements such as security. It includes all the design elements needed to define or refine the statistical products or services identified in the business case. This phase specifies all relevant metadata, in accordance with the standards and corporate policies, ready for use later in the business process, as well as quality assurance procedures. For statistical outputs produced on a regular basis, this phase usually occurs for the first iteration and whenever improvement actions are identified in the Evaluate phase of a previous iteration. Design activities make substantial use of international and national standards in order to reduce the length and cost of the design process, and enhance interoperability, comparability, etc. Organisations may reuse or adapt design elements from existing processes and consider geospatial aspects of data in the design to enhance the usability and value of the statistical information. Additionally, outputs of design processes may form the basis for future standards at the organisational, national or international levels. The Design phase is broken down into six sub-processes (Figure 8), which are presented sequentially, from left to right, but can also occur in parallel, and can be iterative. Some approaches used to develop tools and systems involve iteration between sub-processes in the Design and Build phases.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This role leads methodological design and development for surveys and statistical programs, including statistical outputs, variables, methodologies and processes. It is responsible for researching and refining design elements, developing and disseminating good practice, coordinating methodological standards work, and supporting quality assurance. Sample: 'Leads interdisciplinary teams to conduct development work on new statistical and survey methods', 'Conducts research, develops new methods and/or refines existing methods and techniques of survey design, data collection, processing and data analysis, and identifies potential benefits of applying the methods in terms of cost, timeliness and quality for existing or new surveys.' The involvement in system, method, and output design as well as quality assurance directly links to the functions of the Design phase.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Mathematics (Survey Methodology Lead)

implicated work-descriptions.justification: This position coordinates and organizes design activities for dissemination, data processing, editing, and validation; implements changes to processes and systems; ensures subject-matter requirements and international/national standards are developed and translated into specifications. Key tasks include: 'Recommends improvements to statistical methods and procedures and implements changes to processing systems and applications...', 'Liaises with subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development, to suggest improvements to ongoing programs, and to establish project plans and target dates.' These responsibilities support the broad design, refinement, and standardization needs of this phase.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator

implicated work-descriptions.justification: Responsible for planning, coordinating and implementing the design of collection instruments, overseeing methodological research, ensuring the application of standards, integrating metadata and security considerations in system design, and leading technical teams in developing operational solutions. From its description: 'Develops proposals and provides advice regarding changes and improvements on questionnaire design; enhancements or modifications to survey content and coverage; revisions to collection systems and processes, and the implementation of new hardware and software to be used in data collection activities.' This role ensures that all practical research and development activities for statistical production and integration of metadata and security take place at the design stage.
implicated work-descriptions.title: District Manager, Regional Operations (Data Collection)

implicated work-descriptions.justification: Analyzes, documents and recommends procedures for quality assurance, supervises the design of operational procedures, and coordinates activities relating to the definition and review of standards and procedures for data validation/editing. Example: 'Writes program information manuals, training packages, monitoring procedures and management reports for use by colleagues, operational staff and management in the development, implementation and assessment of statistical programs.' and 'Delivers specialized training to colleagues and other data users within the department.' The involvement in specifying and promoting quality and metadata standards makes this role fundamental to the Design phase.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator

title: Design outputs and dissemination
description: This sub-process contains the detailed design of the statistical outputs, products and services to be produced, including the related systems, tools and procedures used in the Disseminate phase. Processes governing access to any confidential outputs are also designed here. Outputs should be designed to follow existing standards wherever possible, so inputs to this process may include metadata from similar or previous collections (including extractions from statistical, administrative, geospatial and other non-statistical registers and databases), international standards, and information about practices in other statistical organisations from sub-process 1.1 (Identify needs). Outputs may also be designed in partnership with other interested bodies, particularly if they are considered to be joint outputs, or they will be disseminated by another organisation.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Production and Database Expert is responsible for developing, maintaining, and supporting production and dissemination processes and outputs for analytical databases. The activities explicitly include the innovation, implementation, evaluation and testing of processes for the manipulation, storage, and retrieval of statistical data, which directly supports the detailed design of statistical outputs and dissemination systems. For example: 'Develops and maintains production and dissemination processes and outputs for analytical databases and provides support for tools and systems for the delivery of high-impact statistical programs, new products, special studies, and ad hoc requests.' and 'Integrates input from multiple economic subject matter areas to develop and maintain complex systems and frameworks for the ongoing production, validation and dissemination of a range of specialized, high-impact statistical outputs.'
implicated work-descriptions.title: Production and Database Expert

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Data Production and Dissemination Development Officer develops processing systems/applications and designs system specifications for testing and database maintenance—which is essential for the design and implementation of systems/tools required for output and dissemination. Furthermore, the role communicates technical specifications to both users and development teams: 'Develops processing systems and applications used to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data.' and 'Designs specifications for the testing of data and for the maintenance and development of databases.'
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Development Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator coordinates and organizes the editing, validation, marketing, and dissemination of data, recommends improvements and implements changes to statistical methods and procedures and ensures subject matter requirements are translated into system specifications. This includes providing subject matter advice on the design of outputs/data products and the use of standards: 'Coordinates and organizes the retrieval, editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of data.' and 'Liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development, to suggest improvements to ongoing programs, and to establish project plans and target dates.'
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator

title: Design variables
description: This sub-process defines the variables to be collected via the collection instrument, as well as any other variables that will be derived from them in sub-process 5.5 (Derive new variables and units), and any statistical or geospatial classifications that will be used. This is also where unit types (including observation units and statistical units) can be designed. It is expected that existing national and international standards will be followed wherever possible. This sub-process may need to run in parallel with sub-process 2.3 (Design collection), as the definition of the variables to be collected and the choice of collection instruments may be inter-dependent to some degree. Preparation of metadata for collected and derived variables, statistical and geospatial classification is a necessary precondition for subsequent phases.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator is responsible for analyzing and determining the relevance of current collection and presentation methods, proposing new or alternative systems, writing and explaining subject matter and technical concepts and definitions, and advising on the development of statistical databases. This is directly implicated in defining and specifying variables, classifications, and associated metadata. Examples: 'Analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems,' and 'Writes and presents detailed subject matter and technical concepts, definitions and terms in common terminology in order to explain and clarify divisional systems and applications.'1
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Section Chief, Statistical Program Development leads development and evaluation regarding data collection, coding, processing, and the integration of data from a variety of sources. They resolve data conflicts, define program requirements for statistical data, and are also responsible for identifying subject-matter concept and definition requirements. Direct evidence: 'Identifies program requirements for statistical data, determines new or modified data items to be collected, and recommends changes to collection methodology and/or output definitions.' and 'Knowledge of the concepts, methods and techniques used in the collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of statistical data in order to advise on subject-matter development and resolve subject-matter concept and definition issues.'2
implicated work-descriptions.title: Section Chief, Statistical Program Development

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Data Analytics and Integration Officer is responsible for providing subject matter advice regarding subject-matter concepts, defining requirements for new data items, and developing and coordinating integration projects, which includes developing metadata for new and derived variables and ensuring alignment with standards. Example: 'Provides subject matter advice and direction to users on matters relating to subject-matter concepts used in the development and operation of a statistical database,' and 'Knowledge of current or emerging economic and social issues relating to the program area in order to identify subject-matter concept and definition requirements.'3
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Analytics and Integration Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The District Manager, Regional Operations (Data Collection) manages the work of the district office related to collection activities, provides proposals and advice regarding questionnaire design, survey content, and system definition, and identifies developments in collection concepts, methods, and response patterns, which directly informs variable definition and design. Example: 'Develops proposals and provides advice regarding changes and improvements on questionnaire design; enhancements or modifications to survey content and coverage.'4
implicated work-descriptions.title: District Manager, Regional Operations (Data Collection)

title: Design collection
description: This sub-process prepares a collection strategy for the data, and determines the most appropriate collection instruments and methods, which may depend on the type of data collection, the collection unit type (enterprise, person, or other) and the available sources of data. The actual activities in this sub-process will vary according to the type of collection instrument required, which can include computer assisted interviewing, paper questionnaires, administrative registers, automated and semi-automated data transfer methods (such as using APIs, machine-to-machine integrations and various types of file transfers), web-scraping technologies as well as technology for geospatial data. The collection may employ a multi-mode method which requires additional considerations such as design of sequencing or different instruments for different modes. Direct or indirect use of administrative data may be introduced in the data collection mode for either controlling survey data or assisting it when capturing survey information. In the case of survey (or census) data, this collection strategy includes the design of the collection instruments, questions and response templates (in conjunction with the variables and statistical classifications designed in sub-process 2.2 (Design variables)). It is important to understand respondents and incorporate the user perspectives in the design of data collection. This sub-process may include design of fieldwork operations, and respondent engagement, in the case of survey data collection. It also includes the confirmation of existing agreements or creation of new agreements. This sub-process is enabled by tools such as question libraries (to facilitate the reuse of questions and related attributes), questionnaire tools (to enable the quick and easy compilation of questions into formats suitable for cognitive testing) and agreement templates (to help standardise terms and conditions). This sub-process also includes the design of respondent management systems that are specific to this business process. Where statistical organisations do not collect data directly (i.e. a third party controls the collection and processing of the data), this sub-process may include the design of mechanisms to monitor the data and the metadata to assess impacts of any change made by the third party.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Mathematics (Survey Methodology Lead, MA-04) role leads the design and development of survey and data collection strategy, including the creation of collection instruments, questionnaire design (for paper and computer applications), cognitive testing, collection planning, development of automated and manual data transfer methods, and respondent engagement approaches. It provides end-to-end expertise for both method choice and instrument construction—including: 'Principles and methods of questionnaire design for both paper and computerized applications and knowledge of cognitive methods of testing questionnaires to design collection documents and related training and operational manuals.' and 'Data collection methods to design questionnaires and training manuals, to design sampling schemes, to design pilot surveys, and to design components of data collection systems.' This matches precisely the sub-process's requirement for comprehensive collection instrument and method design, use of new technology, and respondent engagement.12345
implicated work-descriptions.title: Mathematics (Survey Methodology Lead)

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The District Manager, Regional Operations (Data Collection, EC-06) manages collection operations, designs questionnaire and collection instrument modifications, implements fieldwork operations, and oversees pilot testing and respondent management. Core activities include: 'Develops proposals and provides advice regarding changes and improvements on questionnaire design; enhancements or modifications to survey content and coverage; revisions to collection systems and processes, and the implementation of new hardware and software to be used in data collection activities.' and 'Manages the work of the district office related to collection activities.' This directly supports complex collection design and adaptation with respondent and operational focus.6
implicated work-descriptions.title: District Manager, Regional Operations (Data Collection)

title: Design frame and sample
description: This sub-process applies especially to processes which involve data collection based on sampling, such as through statistical surveys, but it may also apply to other types of data collection such as census or register-based (e.g., filtering of registers based on the target population). It identifies and specifies the population of interest, defines a sampling frame (and, where necessary, the register from which it is derived), and determines the most appropriate sampling criteria and methodology (which could include complete enumeration). Common sources for a sampling frame are administrative and statistical registers, censuses and information from other sample surveys. It may refer to geospatial data and classifications. This sub-process describes how these sources can be combined if needed. Analysis of whether the frame covers the target population should be performed. Spatial analysis techniques can be used to ensure the spatial distribution of the units is appropriate. A sampling plan should be made. The actual sample is created in sub-process 4.1 (Create frame and select sample), using the methodology specified in this sub-process.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Mathematics (MA-02/MA-04) roles are directly implicated as they are responsible for designing sampling frames and sample schemes, defining sampling strategies, determining and allocating sample sizes, and preparing technical notes on data quality and sampling methodology. Evidence: 'Develops sample frames and sampling schemes', 'Probability theory and statistical inference to design sampling frames and sample schemes and to conduct analytical and evaluation studies.', 'Survey sampling methods including: use and maintenance of sampling frames, stratification, sample size determination and allocation, sample selection, multistage sampling, multiphase sampling, area sampling, sample rotation, weighting and estimation, variance estimation, use of modelling, and techniques to measure and assess sampling and non-sampling errors in surveys.' These responsibilities directly meet the methodological requirements of identifying the population of interest, developing the frame, designing sampling criteria and methodology, and creating/managing the sampling plan, including the possible use of geospatial approaches and combining sources. The roles also conduct evaluation studies to assess frame coverage and sampling quality.123456789101112
implicated work-descriptions.title: Mathematics (Survey Methodologist, Sampling Specialist)

title: Design processing and analysis
description: This sub-process designs the statistical methodology to be applied during the Process and Analyse phases. This can include, among others, specification of routines and rules for coding, editing and imputation, which may vary based on the means of data collection and source of data. This subprocess also includes design of specifications for data integration from multiple data sources, validation of data and estimation. Statistical disclosure control methods are also designed here if they are specific to this business process.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Mathematics (Survey Methodologist, MA-02/MA-03/MA-04) roles are core for designing all processing and analysis routines, including specification of rules for coding, editing, and imputation; development of methods for estimation and variance estimation; integrating data from multiple sources; and quality assurance of analysis methodology. These positions develop and adapt processing specifications, automated coding and imputation systems, design and test new analysis routines, and prepare detailed methodological documentation—all precisely aligning to the sub-process tasks. Evidence includes: 'Develops methods and specifications for coding, editing and imputation,' 'Develops and adapts procedures and practices in the processing of survey data to abide by disclosure provisions,' 'Prepares comprehensive reports detailing proposed procedures and methodologies,' 'Research on new methods and techniques of data collection, processing and analysis,' and 'Ensuring compliance with confidentiality and disclosure provisions.' The role also provides technical guidance to ensure processing and methodological standards are met across processing, integration, and disclosure control operations12345678.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Mathematics (Survey Methodologist/Research, Sampling/Processing/Analysis Specialist)

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Data Analytics and Integration Officer (EC-05) is responsible for developing recommendations, providing advice, and implementing new processing and analysis methodologies (including integration, modeling, validation, and data analytics). The role oversees technical projects, participates in data integration negotiations, and has in-depth knowledge of statistical principles and data analysis tools, which is essential for developing the specifications for how data will be processed, analyzed, coded, edited, and integrated in the later phases. For example: 'Develops recommendations, provides advice to management and implements initiatives pertaining to new methods of acquiring, processing, modeling, analyzing or disseminating data to meet user needs.' and 'Knowledge of methods and techniques used in research, evaluation, manipulation, integration, analysis and dissemination of statistical data. This may include machine learning and other skills related to big data.'9
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Analytics and Integration Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Section Chief, Statistical Program Development (EC-05) plays a vital role in reviewing and approving processing parameters, classification/coding/report formats, resolving technical and conceptual processing issues, and developing specifications for new/existing data compilation programs. The role coordinates operations and assesses the impact of new processing methodologies, which supports all aspects of the processing and analysis design phase, including data validation routines and integration. For example: 'Reviews and approves detailed processing parameters, classification, coding systems and report formats or develops new ones to meet specific needs' and 'Reviews new and revised processing systems and procedures to ensure compatibility with other statistical programs. Assesses technical and conceptual problems and inconsistencies in the manipulation, storage and retrieval of statistical data and develops specifications for new and existing data compilation programs.'10
implicated work-descriptions.title: Section Chief, Statistical Program Development

title: Design production systems and workflows
description: This sub-process determines the workflow from data collection to dissemination, taking an overview of all the processes required within the whole production process and ensuring that they fit together efficiently with no gaps or redundancies. Various systems and databases may be needed throughout the process. The GSBPM can be used to design a statistical organisation’s business architecture layer when a statistical organisation has an existing enterprise architecture in place. The design might be adjusted to fit the organisation. A general principle is to reuse processes and technology across many statistical business processes, so existing production solutions (e.g. services, systems and databases) should be examined first, to determine whether they are fit for purpose for this specific production process, then, if any gaps are identified, new solutions can be designed. This sub-process also considers how staff will interact with systems and who will be responsible for what and when.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Production and Database Expert (EC-05) is explicitly responsible for developing and maintaining complex systems and frameworks for the ongoing production, validation, and dissemination of a range of specialized, high-impact statistical outputs. Key activities include coordinating activities of multiple departmental and external partners, operationalizing measurement frameworks in systems and databases, developing guidelines for design, evaluation, and testing of processing systems and applications, and recommending and implementing modifications and improvements to existing procedures. These responsibilities cover the design of workflows, system integration, and ensuring efficient fit and interoperability across production process steps. For example: 'Defines project objectives and priorities, prepares work plans and summaries outlining approaches, time-frames, and resources ... Reviews and approves detailed processing parameters, devises criteria and methods to rectify inconsistencies, and recommends modifications to ensure the continuity and compatibility of data ... Integrates input from multiple economic subject matter areas to develop and maintain complex systems and frameworks for the ongoing production, validation and dissemination of a range of specialized, high-impact statistical outputs.'
implicated work-descriptions.title: Production and Database Expert

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator (EC-03) coordinates and organizes operational systems and process improvements, leads the re-design of processing applications, develops system specifications, and leads the implementation and assessment phases for statistical programs. They are also responsible for translating requirements into system specs, proposing new or alternative systems, and ensuring all components work smoothly together, which is directly aligned to workflow and production system design described in this sub-process. Example: 'Liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development, to suggest improvements to ongoing programs, and to establish project plans and target dates ... Recommends improvements to statistical methods and procedures and implements changes to processing systems and applications to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data.'
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator

title: Build
description: This phase builds and tests the production solution to the point where it is ready for use in the “live” environment. The outputs of the Design phase are assembled and configured in this phase to create the complete operational environment to run the process. New services are built by exception, created in response to gaps in the existing catalogue of services sourced from within the organisation and externally. These new services are constructed to be broadly reusable in alignment with the business architecture of the organisation where possible, and compliant with security requirements. For statistical outputs produced on a regular basis, this phase usually occurs for the first iteration, following a review or a change in methodology or technology, rather than for every iteration. The Build phase is broken down into seven sub-processes (Figure 9), which are presented sequentially, from left to right, but can also occur in parallel, and can be iterative. Some approaches used to develop tools and systems involve iteration between sub-processes in the Design and Build phases. The first three sub-processes are concerned with the development and improvement of systems used in collection, processing, analysis and dissemination of data. The last four subprocesses focus on the end-to-end process.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Production and Database Expert (EC-05) is responsible for the innovation, implementation, evaluation, assembly, and technical deployment of new or improved production and dissemination systems and processes, taking technical designs from the Design phase into live or test production. This includes development and configuration of tools and frameworks for data processing, integration, validation, and dissemination; supporting migration to live operations; reviewing and ensuring production-readiness; managing implementation and operationalization of new or revised technical systems; and leading the deployment and testing of major changes. Key activities are: 'Innovates and implements the design, evaluation, and applications for the manipulation, storage, and retrieval of high-impact statistical data.', 'Develops and maintains production and dissemination processes and outputs for analytical databases and provides support for tools and systems for the delivery of high-impact statistical programs, new products, special studies, and ad hoc requests.', 'Coordinates activities of multiple Statistic Canada divisional partners and other external partners to process, validate, and disseminate statistical data.', 'Leads project teams and undertakes complex technical projects in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems.' These responsibilities directly match all core Build phase requirements.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Production and Database Expert

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator (EC-03) is responsible for assembling, organizing, and implementing changes to production systems, testing and validating new and updated applications, coordinating implementation of new systems, training users, providing technical documentation, and providing support for production deployment of new workflows or applications—core Build activities. Evidence includes: 'Implements changes to processing systems and applications to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data.', 'Provides subject matter advice and direction to users on matters relating to subject-matter concepts.', 'Writes program information manuals, training packages, monitoring procedures and management reports for use by colleagues, operational staff and management in the development, implementation and assessment of statistical programs.', 'Delivers specialized training to colleagues and other data users within the department.' These activities map directly to the need to assemble, configure, test, and move systems/services into the production environment.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator

title: Reuse or build collection instruments
description: This sub-process describes the activities to build and reuse the collection instruments needed during the Collect phase. The collection instruments are built based on the design specifications created during the Design phase. A collection may use one or more collection instruments to receive the data (e.g. personal or telephone interviews; paper, electronic or web questionnaires; SDMX web services). Collection instruments may also be data extraction routines used to gather data from existing statistical or administrative registers (e.g. by using existing service interfaces). This sub-process also includes preparing and testing the contents and functioning of that collection instrument (e.g. cognitive testing of the questions in a questionnaire). It is recommended to consider the direct connection of collection instruments to a metadata system, so that metadata can be more easily captured in the collection phase. Connecting metadata and data at the point of capture can save work in later phases. Capturing the metrics of data collection (paradata) is also an important consideration in this sub-process for calculating and analysing process quality indicators.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Mathematics (Survey Methodologist, MA-03/MA-04) roles develop and refine collection instruments (including questionnaires for both paper and computer-assisted modes), perform and oversee cognitive testing, pilot test surveys, and document the process and methodology. The roles specify and test components for data collection systems and ensure systems are ready for operational deployment. Activities include: 'Principles and methods of questionnaire design for both paper and computerized applications and knowledge of cognitive methods of testing questionnaires to design collection documents and related training and operational manuals.' and 'Designs and develops pilot tests to assess performance of components under study; determines the appropriate information required to support the development of the component.' This encompasses the breadth of activities in this sub-process: construction, reuse, and thorough testing of collection instruments, as well as system integration for collection and paradata capture. These responsibilities are documented with further detail and explicit linkage to survey methods, document preparation, evaluation, reporting, and training/support for users and clients123456.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Mathematics (Survey Methodologist, Questionnaire & Collection Instrument Specialist)

title: Reuse or build processing and analysis components
description: This sub-process describes the activities to reuse existing components or build new components needed for the Process and Analyse phases, as designed in the Design phase. Services (re-)used may include dashboard functions and features, information services, transformation functions, geospatial data services, workflow management tools, respondent and metadata management services.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Production and Database Expert (EC-05) leads the innovation, implementation, development, and technical deployment of new or improved statistical processing and analysis systems that will ultimately be used in the operational environment. Relevant activities span developing and maintaining processing and dissemination processes, building analytical databases, implementing quality assurance routines, integrating input from multiple subject matter areas, executing solutions to technical processing challenges, developing guidelines for design, evaluation and testing of processing systems, and coordinating with a range of partners to deliver these solutions. This breadth of responsibility includes all core elements of the Build phase for processing and analysis components: 'Innovates and implements the design, evaluation, and applications for the manipulation, storage, and retrieval of high-impact statistical data.'; 'Develops and maintains production and dissemination processes and outputs for analytical databases and provides support for tools and systems for the delivery of high-impact statistical programs, new products, special studies, and ad hoc requests.'; 'Coordinates activities of multiple Statistic Canada divisional partners and other external partners to process, validate, and disseminate statistical data.'; 'Leads project teams and undertakes complex technical projects in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems.'1.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Production and Database Expert

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator (EC-03) is responsible for assembling, organizing, implementing, and supporting new and existing statistical processing systems and applications, including those for editing, validation, mining, retrieval, and storage. Relevant activities include coordinating improvements to systems, guiding implementation of new processing routines, and providing user support for new tools: 'Recommends improvements to statistical methods and procedures and implements changes to processing systems and applications to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data.'; 'Coordinates and organizes the retrieval, editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of data.'; 'Writes program information manuals, training packages, monitoring procedures and management reports for use by colleagues, operational staff and management in the development, implementation and assessment of statistical programs.' These responsibilities make this role fundamental in the (re)building and maintenance of the processing and analysis components needed for modern statistical production. 2
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator

title: Reuse or build dissemination components
description: This sub-process describes the activities to build new components or reuse existing components needed for the dissemination of statistical products as designed in sub-process 2.1 (Design outputs and dissemination). All types of dissemination components are included, from those that produce traditional paper publications to those that provide web services, (linked) open data outputs, geospatial statistics, maps, or access to microdata.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Production and Database Expert (EC-05) is explicitly responsible for developing and implementing production and dissemination processes and outputs for analytical databases, and supporting tools and systems for delivery of statistical programs such as new products, special studies, and ad hoc requests. The role includes bringing new dissemination solutions into production in coordination with partners, resolving technical issues, designing and evaluating system changes, and providing guidance and support for the delivery of outputs (e.g., databases, web tools, dynamic products, open data). This closely aligns with the needs of this sub-process to build and reuse all types of dissemination components irrespective of output format. For example: 'Develops and maintains production and dissemination processes and outputs for analytical databases and provides support for tools and systems for the delivery of high-impact statistical programs, new products, special studies, and ad hoc requests.' and 'Coordinates activities of multiple Statistic Canada divisional partners and other external partners to process, validate, and disseminate statistical data.'
implicated work-descriptions.title: Production and Database Expert

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator (EC-03) coordinates the preparation, validation, and delivery of data and products across platforms and ensures data and metadata are disseminated as expected. The role provides system and product documentation, custom tabulations for clients, and manages changes or enhancements to the dissemination process. This matches sub-process needs concerning managing a range of dissemination channels and formats, and supporting the operationalization of new or revised output dissemination modules. Supporting statements include: 'Coordinates and organizes the retrieval, editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of data.' and 'Provides custom tabulations and time-series information for ad-hoc client requests.' and 'Writes program information manuals, training packages, monitoring procedures and management reports for use by colleagues, operational staff and management in the development, implementation and assessment of statistical programs.'
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator

title: Configure workflows
description: This sub-process configures the workflows, systems and transformations used within the business processes, from data collection through to dissemination. In this sub-process, the workflows are configured based on the design created in sub-process 2.6 (Design production systems and workflows). This could include modifying a standardised workflow for a specific purpose, assembling the workflows for the different phases together (possibly with a workflow/business process management system) and configuring systems accordingly.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Production and Database Expert (EC-05) is responsible for integrating and assembling workflow components for end-to-end statistical processes, developing and maintaining production systems, and coordinating the activities of various partners across all phases. This includes defining project objectives, integrating input from multiple subject areas, developing technical solutions to assemble processing workflows, and ensuring the compatibility and efficiency of systems used for collection, processing, analysis, and dissemination. Descriptions from the source include: 'Integrates input from multiple economic subject matter areas to develop and maintain complex systems and frameworks for the ongoing production, validation and dissemination of a range of specialized, high-impact statistical outputs.' and 'Coordinates activities of multiple Statistic Canada divisional partners and other external partners.' These activities explicitly match with configuring workflows for multiple phases and systems to deliver efficient, unified production solutions.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Production and Database Expert

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator (EC-03) oversees operational workflows, including implementing and coordinating system changes, assembling workflows for business processes, and ensuring system configuration aligns with project requirements. The role documents and communicates workflow arrangements to operational staff and other stakeholders. Key support: 'Coordinates and organizes the retrieval, editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of data.' and 'Implements changes to processing systems and applications to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data.' These responsibilities demonstrate comprehensive involvement in configuring and assembling workflow solutions across the statistical process.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator

title: Test production systems
description: This sub-process is concerned with the testing of assembled and configured services and related workflows. It includes technical testing and sign-off of new programmes and routines, as well as confirmation that existing routines from other statistical business processes are suitable for use in this case. Whilst part of this activity concerning the testing of individual components and services could logically be linked with sub-processes 3.1 (Reuse or build collection instruments), 3.2 (Reuse or build processing and analysis components) and 3.3 (Reuse or build dissemination components), this sub-process also includes testing of interactions between assembled and configured services and ensuring that the whole production solution works in a coherent way.
