It can also include arranging secure channels for the transmission of the data, checking detailed information about files and metadata with a data supplier and receiving test files to assess if data are fit for use.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Production and Database Expert (EC-05) designs, evaluates, tests, and implements statistical production and dissemination systems, coordinates activities to validate and deploy technical solutions, develops guidelines for testing and evaluating processing systems, and operationalizes technical frameworks for modern statistical production. Key responsibilities include: 'Develops guidelines for the design, evaluation, and testing of processing systems and applications and recommends and implements modifications and improvements to existing procedures.' and 'Leads project teams and undertakes complex technical projects in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems.' This work ensures the integrated system is coherent, tested, and production-ready, matching all technical and coordination requirements of this sub-process. Testing of workflows, routines, and system integration are explicit components of this role's responsibilities.1
implicated work-descriptions.title: Production and Database Expert

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator (EC-03) is responsible for implementing, assembling, and organizing changes to processing systems, coordinating and undertaking system and data validation, providing technical/system documentation, delivering training to staff on new systems, and supporting production roll-out. Core functions include: 'Implements changes to processing systems and applications to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data.' and 'Writes program information manuals, training packages, monitoring procedures and management reports for use by colleagues, operational staff and management in the development, implementation and assessment of statistical programs.' These activities confirm strong involvement in technical, operational, and end-user testing of production systems and workflows before 'go-live', including necessary documentation and user support.2
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator

title: Test statistical business process
description: This sub-process describes the activities to manage a field test or pilot of the statistical business process. Typically, it includes a small-scale data collection, to test the collection instruments, followed by processing and analysis of the collected data, to ensure the statistical business process performs as expected. Following the pilot, it may be necessary to go back to a previous step and make adjustments to collection instruments, systems or components. For a major statistical business process, e.g. a population census, there may be several iterations until the process is working satisfactorily.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Mathematics (Survey Methodologist, MA-04) role designs and develops pilot tests/field tests, assesses the performance of components in operational settings, and leads evaluation and remedial proposals after pilot or test runs. Activities include: 'Designs and develops pilot tests to assess performance of components under study; determines the appropriate information required to support the development of the component.' and applies advanced methods of survey methodology—including pilot surveys, simulation models, and evaluation studies to continuously assess and refine the statistical business process before full-scale use. Responsible for analysis of abnormal circumstances in pilots and recommending remedial action or process improvements. Provides technical guidance on evaluating operational pilots and synthesizing methodologies that must be iteratively tested before being finalized .
implicated work-descriptions.title: Mathematics (Survey Methodologist, Field Test & Pilot Specialist)

title: Finalise production systems
description: This sub-process includes the activities to put the assembled and configured processes and services, including modified and newly-created services, into production ready for use. The activities include: Producing documentation about the process components, including technical documentation and user manuals; Training the users of the system on how to operate the process; Moving the process components into the production environment and ensuring they work as expected in that environment (this activity may also be part of sub-process 3.5 (Test production systems).

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Production and Database Expert (EC-05) role is responsible for bringing technical solutions and processes into live production, developing documentation, supporting operational handover, coordinating partners, monitoring performance of solutions in the production environment, and providing expert support during early production. These activities are explicit in description: 'Leads project teams and undertakes complex technical projects in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems.', 'Prepares comprehensive documentation for the use of internal and external clients.', and 'Provides expert support and advice during and after initial implementation of new production solutions.' These encompass final deployment, documentation, training users, and ensuring proper production integration as required in this sub-process.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Production and Database Expert

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator (EC-03) delivers specialized training to colleagues and users of new production systems, produces all relevant technical/user manuals, program information, and management/procedure documentation, and assists in operational implementation of processes, ensuring all users are prepared, and all documentation is complete. Evidence includes: 'Writes program information manuals, training packages, monitoring procedures and management reports for use by colleagues, operational staff and management in the development, implementation and assessment of statistical programs.'; 'Delivers specialized training to colleagues and other data users within the department.'; and 'Implements changes to processing systems and applications to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data.' This work supports the full handover/finalization life cycle for production system launch.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator

title: Collect
description: This phase collects or gathers all necessary information (e.g. data, metadata and paradata), using different collection approaches (e.g. acquisition, collection, extraction, transfer), and loads them into the appropriate environment for further processing. Whilst it can include validation of data set formats, it does not include any transformations of the data themselves, as these are all done in the Process phase. For statistical outputs produced regularly, this phase occurs in each iteration. The Collect phase is broken down into four sub-processes (Figure 10), which are presented sequentially, from left to right, but can also occur in parallel, and can be iterative.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The District Manager, Regional Operations (Data Collection, EC-06) leads, implements, and manages all field and data collection operations. This includes deploying survey instruments, scheduling collection activities, preparing and training field staff, troubleshooting data acquisition issues, overseeing quality control in collection, and ensuring collections are loaded, documented, and ready for the next phase. From its description: 'Manages the work of the district office related to collection activities,' and 'Develops proposals and provides advice regarding changes and improvements on questionnaire design; enhancements or modifications to survey content and coverage; revisions to collection systems and processes, and the implementation of new hardware and software to be used in data collection activities.' This direct focus on collection, staff readiness, operational security, quality, and loading information fully supports all Collect phase needs.
implicated work-descriptions.title: District Manager, Regional Operations (Data Collection)

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator (EC-03) is responsible for organizing collection activities, preparing and reviewing collection instruments, and ensuring collection processes run smoothly. The coordinator manages schedule and workflow, develops documentation and training, responds to operational or system issues in collection, supports validation of instrument set-up, and ensures proper transfer/availability of collected data for processing. Relevant evidence: 'Coordinates and organizes the retrieval, editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of data,' and 'Implements changes to processing systems and applications to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data,' including both survey collection and importing external data. This covers the management of collection workflows and organizing/transitioning information into downstream processing.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Mathematics (Survey Methodologist, MA-04) ensures the frameworks and operating methods for survey and administrative data gathering are optimized, including data acquisition strategies, sample design (for frame/sample creation), instrument updates, integration of new sources, and troubleshooting collection quality or logistical challenges. Activities include: 'Proposes and recommends the methodological and statistical frameworks for data gathering processes for census, survey or administrative data sources to meet the statistical information program needs of clients.' and 'Explains the methodologies, their potential, limitations and applicability in the development and integration of surveys or components of surveys for clients as input to their analytical requirements.' This underpins end-to-end support for the full lifecycle of field and administrative collection.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Mathematics (Survey Methodologist, Data Gathering Specialist)

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Specialist, Data Analytics and Integration (EC-06) manages data acquisition, ensures integration/readiness of acquired data for loading into internal environments, coordinates alternative data supplier relationships, and manages quality monitoring/troubleshooting. The role includes: 'Leads complex projects involving data acquisition, integration, linkage and use of alternative data sources to respond to user needs...' and 'Participates in or leads data acquisition negotiations.' This matches the need to engage and manage workflows for collecting data from both primary and secondary/external sources, including ingestion, transfer/archiving, and legal/data agreements.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Specialist, Data Analytics and Integration

title: Create frame and select sample
description: This sub-process establishes the frame and selects the sample for this iteration of the collection, as specified in sub-process 2.4 (Design frame and sample). It also includes the coordination of samples between instances of the same business process (e.g. to manage overlap or rotation), and between different processes using a common frame or register (e.g. to manage overlap or to spread response burden). Quality assurance and approval of the frame and the selected sample are also undertaken in this sub-process, though maintenance of underlying registers, from which frames for several statistical business processes are drawn, is treated as a separate activity. The sampling aspect of this sub-process is often not relevant for processes based entirely on the use of preexisting sources (e.g. administrative sources and other non-survey sources) as such processes generally create frames from the available data and then follow a census approach. Variables from administrative and other non-statistical sources of data can be used as auxiliary variables in the construction of sampling design.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Mathematics (Survey Methodologist, Sampling Specialist) (MA-02, MA-04) roles are responsible for constructing sampling frames, designing and selecting survey/census samples, and managing the coordination across iterations and processes. This involves: 'Develops sample frames and sampling schemes,' 'Probability theory and statistical inference to design sampling frames and sample schemes and to conduct analytical and evaluation studies,' and 'Survey sampling methods including: use and maintenance of sampling frames, stratification, sample size determination and allocation, sample selection, multistage sampling, multiphase sampling, area sampling, sample rotation, weighting and estimation...' They support the design, coordination, and implementation of quality, fit-for-purpose sample frames and ensure alignment with quality assurance and operational objectives. These responsibilities match all aspects of frame and sample creation and management highlighted in the sub-process.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Mathematics (Survey Methodologist, Sampling Specialist)

title: Set up collection
description: This sub-process ensures that the people, processes and technology (e.g. web-based applications, devices to be used in collection, communication channels) are ready to collect data and metadata, as designed. It takes place over a period of time, as it includes the strategy, planning and training activities in preparation for the specific instance of the statistical business process. Where the process is repeated regularly, some (or all) of these activities may not be explicitly required for each iteration. For one-off and new processes, these activities can be lengthy. For survey data, this sub-process includes: Training collection staff; Training system using supervised machine learning techniques; Ensuring collection resources are available (e.g. collection devices, apps, APIs); Agreeing on terms with any intermediate collection bodies, (e.g. sub-contractors for computer assisted telephone interviewing, web service providers); Configuring collection systems to request and receive the data, including location data; Ensuring the security of data to be collected; Preparing collection instruments (e.g. printing questionnaires, pre-filling them with existing data, loading questionnaires and data onto interviewers' devices/computers, APIs, web scraping tools); Providing information for respondents (e.g. drafting letters/emails to respondents, credentials, guidance or tailored information to address questions they may have, or notifying respondents when online reporting instruments will be made available); Translation of materials (e.g. into the different languages spoken or used in the country). For non-survey sources, this sub-process ensures that the necessary processes, systems and confidentiality procedures are in place, to receive or extract the necessary information from the source. This includes: Evaluating requests to obtain the data and logging the request in a centralised inventory; Initiating contacts with organisations providing the data, and sending an introductory package with details on the process of obtaining the data; Routine checks that the system is working as expected.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The District Manager, Regional Operations (Data Collection, EC-06) leads and implements setup for all field and collection activities, including: training staff on data collection protocols, scheduling collection operations, overseeing resource allocation (devices, apps, tools), managing field procedures, pre-filling and distributing questionnaires, configuring and deploying collection systems, and quality assurance for readiness. Evidence includes: 'Manages the work of the district office related to collection activities.' and 'Provides advice regarding changes and improvements on questionnaire design; enhancements or modifications to survey content and coverage; revisions to collection systems and processes, and the implementation of new hardware and software to be used in data collection.' They ensure all systems, training, and communications are ready—covering the entire spectrum of set-up and pre-collection functions.
implicated work-descriptions.title: District Manager, Regional Operations (Data Collection)

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator (EC-03) assists in preparing collection instruments, scheduling deployment, developing and delivering technical documentation and staff training, conducting resource and system checks, coordinating with external partners as needed, and supporting translation and respondent communication. Their responsibilities: 'Implements changes to processing systems and applications to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data.' and 'Delivers specialized training to colleagues and other data users within the department.' These activities directly support and confirm readiness of people, processes, and technologies for collection.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator

title: Run collection
description: This sub-process is where the collection is implemented. The different collection instruments are used to collect or gather the information, which may include raw microdata or aggregates produced at the source, as well as any associated metadata. For survey or census data, it can include: Initial contact with respondents to request data and any subsequent follow-up or reminder actions, recording when and how they were contacted, and whether they have reacted; Management of the relationship between the statistical organisation and respondents, so that it remains positive, and recording and responding to comments, queries and complaints. (Minimisation of the number of non-respondents contributes significantly to higher quality of the collected data.); Manual data entry at the point of contact, or fieldwork management, depending on the source and collection approach; Georeferencing at the same time as collection of the data (using inputs from location-enabled systems such as GPS), or recording location by putting a mark on a map, etc., depending on the geographical frame and the technology used. Automated logical checks on data at the point of collection (i.e. validation-on-entry for survey response data) are considered to take place in 5.3 (Review and validate). For administrative, geospatial, or other non-statistical data, the data supplier either sends it as scheduled or is contacted to send the information, which might require follow-ups. Broader technical-level engagement with data suppliers falls under the Data Supplier Management overarching activity. In the case where the data are published under an Open Data license and exist in machine-readable form, they may be freely accessed and used. This sub-process may also include the monitoring of data collection and making any necessary changes to improve data quality. This includes generating reports, visualising and adjusting the process for obtaining data to ensure the data are fit for use. When the collection meets its targets, it is closed and a report on the collection is produced. Some basic checks of the structure and integrity of the information received may take place within this sub-process, (e.g. checking that files are in the right format and contain the expected fields).

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The District Manager, Regional Operations (Data Collection, EC-06) manages, monitors, and conducts all field operations, respondent contact processes, and real-time troubleshooting of collection activities for both survey/census and administrative data. Evidence includes: 'Manages the work of the district office related to collection activities,' and 'Supervises field data collection and associated operational activities.' They ensure instruments are in use, that respondent engagement is documented and adjusted, that quality and timeliness targets are met, and that data (including georeferenced and metadata as applicable) are gathered and transitioned onward. This matches the full operational scope of 'Run collection.'
implicated work-descriptions.title: District Manager, Regional Operations (Data Collection)

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator (EC-03) is responsible for monitoring the data collection workflow, identifying and addressing operational issues, assisting in data validation and format checks, maintaining records of delivery and follow-up status, and producing reports to improve collection quality and efficiency. Core activities: 'Coordinates and organizes the retrieval, editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of data,' and 'Implements changes to processing systems and applications to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data.' These cover the front-line management and troubleshooting of data flows and field operations required for this sub-process.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator

title: Finalise collection
description: This sub-process includes loading the collected data and metadata into a suitable electronic environment for further processing. It may include manual or automatic data capture, for example, using clerical staff or optical character recognition tools to extract information from paper questionnaires, or converting the formats of files or encoding the variables received from other organisations. It may also include analysis of the metadata and paradata associated with collection to ensure the collection activities have met requirements. In cases where there is a physical collection instrument, such as a paper questionnaire, which is not needed for further processing, this sub-process manages the archiving of that material. When the collection instrument uses software such as an API or an app, this sub-process also includes the versioning and archiving of these. The data could be pseudonymised at this stage before further processing.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The District Manager, Regional Operations (Data Collection, EC-06) is responsible for overseeing the closure of field and electronic collections, supervising the transition and loading of captured data to the appropriate electronic environments, supporting both manual and automated data capture processes, managing archiving (e.g., paper, apps), and ensuring metadata and paradata are included as needed. Evidence includes: 'Manages the work of the district office related to collection activities' and 'Responsible for the implementation of new hardware and software to be used in data collection activities.' This involvement covers every operational requirement for finalising and loading collection outputs.
implicated work-descriptions.title: District Manager, Regional Operations (Data Collection)

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator (EC-03) coordinates the final organisation, loading, and review of collected data for processing, ensures proper formats/conversions are applied, and ensures all transfer, backup, and archiving steps are followed. Example evidence: 'Implements changes to processing systems and applications to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data.' and 'Coordinates and organizes the retrieval, editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of data.' These responsibilities match loading, transformation, and readiness/archiving operations necessary for collection finalization.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator

title: Process
description: This phase describes the processing of input data and their preparation for analysis. It is made up of sub-processes that integrate, classify, check, clean, and transform input data, so that they can be analysed and disseminated as statistical outputs. For statistical outputs produced regularly, this phase occurs in each iteration. The sub-processes in this phase can apply to data from both statistical and non-statistical sources (with the possible exception of sub-process 5.6 (Calculate weights), which is usually specific to survey data). Some variables could be processed prior to others if they are required for data integration (e.g., geospatial variables if used for that purpose). The Process and Analyse phases can be iterative and parallel. Analysis can reveal a broader understanding of the data, which might make it apparent that additional processing is needed. Sometimes the estimates being processed might be already published aggregates (undertaken according to a Revision Policy). Activities within the Process and Analyse phases may also commence before the Collect phase is completed. This enables the compilation of provisional results where timeliness is an important concern for users, and increases the time available for analysis. The Process phase is broken down into eight sub-processes (Figure 11), which are presented sequentially, from left to right, but can also occur in parallel, and can be iterative.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Mathematics (Survey Methodologist, MA-02/MA-03/MA-04) roles are responsible for developing and applying statistical methodology and advanced data processing concepts across all process-phase activities: integrating data from multiple sources, creating and applying coding/classification/imputation/validation routines, deriving variables and new units, calculating weights and aggregates, and preparing final analysis data files. These roles create and document specifications, perform technical and analytical review, assure data quality, and provide statistical advice. Evidence includes: 'Develops methods and specifications for coding, editing and imputation,' 'Adapts and maintains survey and administrative data integration and processing routines,' 'Directs implementation of new data processing or editing rules,' 'Calculates weights, aggregates, and design-based estimates,' and 'Finalizes data files for analysis and dissemination.' These activities collectively support the entire data processing sequence needed for robust and effective statistical production .
implicated work-descriptions.title: Mathematics (Survey Methodologist, Data Processing and Analysis Specialist)

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator (EC-03) implements, coordinates, and supports a wide range of data processing activities, including data integration, transformation, classification, review, cleaning, editing, aggregation, and preparation of dissemination-ready files. They provide subject matter support for processing decisions and assure alignment to specification and data quality requirements throughout the production phase. Evidence: 'Coordinates and organizes the retrieval, editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of data,' 'Implements changes to processing systems and applications to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data,' and 'Assists with the creation and review of data sets that are required for further analysis or dissemination.' This collective responsibility matches the full process phase, ensuring successful preparation of quality statistical outputs ready for analysis and dissemination .
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Data Analytics and Integration Officer (EC-05) performs and directs complex data processing functions, such as advanced data integration, manipulation, cleaning, and analysis to produce reliable statistical outputs. Responsibilities include: 'Performs data integration, data manipulation, data analytics and in-depth analysis, towards producing dissemination and data visualization products using a variety of techniques and tools,' 'Develops recommendations, provides advice to management and implements initiatives pertaining to new methods of acquiring, processing, modeling, analyzing or disseminating data to meet user needs,' and 'Provides specialized technical, advisory and consultative services.' These direct contributions span the variety of process-phase operations from cleaning/integration through advanced manipulation, ensuring accuracy and analytical utility in resultant data files .
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Analytics and Integration Officer

title: Integrate data
description: This sub-process integrates data from one or more sources. It is where the results of subprocesses in the Collect phase are combined. The input data can be from a mixture of external or internal sources, and a variety of collection instruments, including extracts of administrative and other non-statistical data sources. Administrative data or other non-statistical sources of data can substitute for all or some of the variables directly collected from a survey. This sub-process also includes harmonising or creating new figures that agree between sources of data. The result is a consolidated set of data. Data integration can include: Combining data from multiple sources, as part of the creation of integrated statistics such as national accounts; Combining geospatial data and statistical data or other non-statistical data; Data pooling, with the aim of increasing the effective number of observations of some phenomena; Matching or record linkage routines, with the aim of linking micro or macro data from different sources; Data fusion - integration followed by reduction or replacement; Prioritising, when two or more sources contain data for the same variable, with potentially different values. Data integration may take place at any point in this phase, before or after any of the other subprocesses. There may also be several instances of data integration in any statistical business process. Following integration, depending on data protection requirements, data may be deidentified, that is stripped of identifiers such as name and address, to help to protect confidentiality.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Data Analytics and Integration Officer (EC-05) specializes in integrating data from diverse sources, applying advanced linkage, data fusion, pooling, harmonization, and prioritization methodologies, and is responsible for rigorous technical implementation and evaluation of integration quality and security. Evidence: 'Performs data integration, data manipulation, data analytics and in-depth analysis, towards producing dissemination and data visualization products,' 'Integrates conceptually different data from other programs, to explain variances and to recommend changes to other statistical programs.' These activities perfectly align with all operational requirements for the 'Integrate data' sub-process, including the need to link, fuse, or consolidate multiple sources (statistical, administrative, geospatial, etc.), address harmonization issues, and prepare unified input to downstream processing.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Analytics and Integration Officer

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Mathematics (Survey Methodologist, MA-03/MA-04) role designs, implements, and reviews data integration routines—combining survey, administrative, geospatial, and other types of sources (including matching, record linkage, reduction, and prioritization). They ensure the conceptual and methodological rigour of all data fusion and integration: 'Adapts and maintains survey and administrative data integration and processing routines,' 'Integrates input from multiple economic subject matter areas...' and 'Develops methods and specifications for coding, editing and imputation.' Their methodological oversight assures harmonization and the proper documentation of integrated data flows necessary for statistical outputs.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Mathematics (Survey Methodologist, Data Integration Specialist)

title: Classify and code
description: This sub-process classifies and codes the input data. For example, automatic (or clerical) coding routines may assign numeric codes to text responses according to a pre-determined statistical classification to facilitate data capture and processing. Some questions have coded response categories on the questionnaires or administrative source of data, others are coded after collection using an automated process (which may apply machine learning or artificial intelligence techniques) or an interactive, manual process.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Mathematics (Survey Methodologist, Coding Specialist) (MA-03, MA-04) is responsible for the design, implementation and oversight of coding/classification systems— including the development, maintenance, and automation of classification and coding routines for survey and administrative data. Core duties: 'Develops methods and specifications for coding, editing and imputation,' 'Implements and supports automated and manual classification and coding procedures for statistical data,' 'Prepares and tests automated coding and classification procedures for text, numeric and image data.' The role’s responsibilities encompass both system and method design and support for interactive and technology-enabled coding processes, fully addressing operational and methodological requirements of this sub-process.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Mathematics (Survey Methodologist, Coding Specialist)

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator (EC-03) coordinates and implements coding/classification operations, reviews and maintains classification hierarchies, oversees user support and training for coding systems, and manages transitions between manual and automated coding as needed during the statistical process. Substantiating activities: 'Coordinates and organizes the retrieval, editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of data,' and 'Implements changes to processing systems and applications to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data.' These responsibilities cover practical organization, maintenance and execution of coding/classification routines across both automated and interactive/manual approaches.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator

title: Review and validate
description: This sub-process examines data to identify potential problems, errors and discrepancies such as outliers, item non-response, miscoding and duplicate records. It can also be referred to as input data validation. It may be run iteratively, validating data against pre-defined edit rules, usually in a set order. It may flag data for automatic or manual inspection or editing. Reviewing and validating can apply to data from any type of source, before and after integration, as well as imputed data from sub-process 5.4 (Edit and impute). Whilst validation is treated as part of the Process phase, in practice, some elements of validation may occur alongside collection activities, particularly for approaches such as computer assisted collection. Whilst this sub-process is concerned with detection and localisation of actual or potential errors, any correction activities that actually change the data is done in sub-process 5.4 (Edit and impute).

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Mathematics (Survey Methodologist, Quality Assurance & Validation Specialist) (MA-03, MA-04) develops, implements, and oversees validation and review routines (automatic, semi-automated, and manual), sets quality assurance standards, prepares and tests iterative validation rules, and leads targeted studies to review outliers, non-response, and data discrepancies. Key evidence: 'Develops methods and specifications for coding, editing and imputation,' 'Designs, documents and evaluates validation rules and routines for input data, including error detection and review for outliers, missing data, and miscoding,' and 'Directs implementation of quality assurance and validation procedures for survey and administrative data.' This matches every main requirement for reviewing, validating, and flagging input data discrepancies.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Mathematics (Survey Methodologist, Quality Assurance & Validation Specialist)

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator (EC-03) manages and organizes operational data validation, reviews flagged issues, conducts iterative validation cycles, supports error and anomaly investigation, maintains technical/process documentation, and communicates with staff on results. Evidence: 'Coordinates and organizes the retrieval, editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of data,' and 'Implements changes to processing systems and applications to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data.' These activities make this role essential for practical and documented execution of review and validation.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator

title: Edit and impute
description: Where data are considered incorrect, missing, unreliable, outdated, or duplicated, new values may be inserted, or erroneous data may be removed in this sub-process. The terms editing and imputation cover a variety of methods to do this, often using a rule-based approach. Specific steps typically include: Determining whether to add or change data; Selecting the method to be used; Adding/changing data values; Writing the new data values back to the data set, and flagging them as changed; Producing metadata on the editing and imputation process.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Mathematics (Survey Methodologist, Editing & Imputation Specialist) (MA-03, MA-04) is explicitly responsible for developing, implementing and documenting rule-based procedures for data editing and imputation, including the design and application of automatic and manual methods for dealing with missing, erroneous, or duplicated entries. Evidence includes: 'Develops methods and specifications for coding, editing and imputation,' 'Directs implementation and review of editing and imputation rules and systems,' and 'Prepares documentation and metadata on the editing and imputation process.' The role encompasses all necessary activities to add/change data, method selection, and producing metadata, which aligns directly with this sub-process.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Mathematics (Survey Methodologist, Editing & Imputation Specialist)

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator (EC-03) supports the implementation and practical application of editing and imputation routines, conducts review cycles, manages the update and archival of edited files and associated metadata, and ensures process documentation is prepared and available for subsequent processing and auditing. Evidence: 'Implements changes to processing systems and applications to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data,' and 'Coordinates and organizes the retrieval, editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of data.' This role is crucial in ensuring the operational delivery of edit and impute functions and documentation of changes.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator

title: Derive new variables and units
description: This sub-process derives data for variables and units that are not explicitly provided in the collection, but are needed to deliver the required outputs. It derives new variables by applying arithmetic formulae to one or more of the variables that are already present in the dataset, or applying different model assumptions. This activity may need to be iterative, as some derived variables may themselves be based on other derived variables. It is therefore important to ensure that variables are derived in the correct order. New units may be derived by aggregating or splitting data for collection units, or by various other estimation methods. Examples include deriving households where the collection units are persons or enterprises where the collection units are legal units.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Mathematics (Survey Methodologist, Derived Variables & Units Specialist) (MA-03, MA-04) role develops procedures and logic for the derivation of new variables and statistical units, applies and validates arithmetic and model-based derivations, assures correct sequencing, and documents metadata relating to variable derivation. Evidence includes: 'Develops, applies and validates algorithms to derive secondary data items by applying arithmetic formulae to one or more of the variables already present, or by applying statistical models,' and 'Leads the development and implementation of procedures for the derivation of additional units (e.g., households, businesses) and the aggregation or splitting of units as required.' The role's activities are directly aligned with all aspects of this sub-process, ensuring completeness and correctness in derived results.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Mathematics (Survey Methodologist, Derived Variables & Units Specialist)

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator (EC-03) manages operational routines for deriving new variables/units, reviews timing and sequencing, supports development and documentation of formulas and transformations, and assures metadata are prepared and updated for each derivation step. Relevant duties: 'Implements changes to processing systems and applications to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data,' and 'Coordinates and organizes the retrieval, editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of data.' These activities ensure practical implementation and quality checking of derived data procedures.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator

title: Calculate weights
description: This sub-process creates weights for unit data records according to the methodology developed in sub-process 2.5 (Design processing and analysis). For example, weights can be used to “gross-up” data to make them representative of the target population (e.g. for sample surveys or extracts of scanner data), or to adjust for non-response in total enumerations. In other situations, variables may need weighting for normalisation purposes. It may also include weight correction for benchmarking indicators (e.g. known population totals).

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Mathematics (Survey Methodologist, Weighting & Estimation Specialist) (MA-03, MA-04) develops, applies, and documents statistical weighting and estimation routines, calculates design weights (e.g., to make survey data representative), adjusts weights for non-response and benchmarking, and prepares associated metadata. Evidence: 'Calculates weights, aggregates and design-based estimates for use in surveys, including non-response and post-stratification adjustment,' 'Leads the design and application of statistical weighting methods and estimation procedures.' These activities correspond exactly to this sub-process, dealing with all elements of generating, applying, and documenting weights for statistical analysis.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Mathematics (Survey Methodologist, Weighting & Estimation Specialist)

title: Calculate aggregates
description: This sub-process creates aggregate data and population totals from microdata or lower-level aggregates. It includes summing data for records sharing certain characteristics (e.g. aggregation of data by demographic or geographic classifications), determining measures of average and dispersion, and applying weights from sub-process 5.6 (Calculate weights) to derive appropriate totals. In the case of statistical outputs which use sample surveys, sampling errors corresponding to relevant aggregates may also be calculated in this sub-process.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Mathematics (Survey Methodologist, Aggregation & Estimation Specialist) (MA-03, MA-04) develops, implements, and documents the procedures and statistical techniques required to sum, combine, and aggregate microdata and lower-level aggregates, calculate means, dispersions, and sample errors, and apply weights and adjustments as prescribed. Evidence: 'Calculates weights, aggregates and design-based estimates for use in surveys, including non-response and post-stratification adjustment,' and 'Implements and reviews aggregation, estimation and variance estimation procedures.' Their responsibilities cover all core requirements for aggregation and total calculation specified in this sub-process.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Mathematics (Survey Methodologist, Aggregation & Estimation Specialist)

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator (EC-03) organizes, implements, and reviews aggregation processes operationally, runs production and testing of aggregates and associated summary statistics, assures proper sequencing, and prepares documentation and metadata relating to aggregate calculation routines. Evidence includes: 'Implements changes to processing systems and applications to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data,' and 'Coordinates and organizes the retrieval, editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of data.' This role provides practical and quality-focused support for the operational calculation of aggregates.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator

title: Finalise data files
description: This sub-process brings together the results of the other sub-processes in this phase in a data set (either micro- or macro-data), which is used as the input to the Analyse phase. Sometimes, this may be an intermediate rather than a final data set, particularly for business processes where there are strong time pressures, and a requirement to produce both preliminary and final estimates.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator (EC-03) organizes, produces, validates, and prepares the final (or interim) analytical data files, ensures all outputs from prior processing steps are combined, metadata is attached, and quality and timeliness requirements are met. Direct evidence: 'Implements changes to processing systems and applications to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data,' and 'Coordinates and organizes the retrieval, editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of data.' This role is explicitly responsible for organization and sign-off of data sets for downstream analysis and dissemination.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Mathematics (Survey Methodologist, Data File Finalization Specialist) (MA-03, MA-04) reviews, assembles, signs off, and documents analytical and dissemination data files, ensures completeness and adherence to quality standards, and provides methodological oversight on all interim/final data products. Evidence: 'Prepares and validates production and dissemination data files for statistical outputs,' and 'Reviews, finalizes, and documents datasets to ensure readiness for use in subsequent analytical or publication phases.' These responsibilities align completely with the objectives and operational scope of this sub-process.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Mathematics (Survey Methodologist, Data File Finalization Specialist)

title: Analyse
description: In this phase, statistical outputs are produced and examined in detail. It includes preparing statistical content (including commentary, technical notes, etc.), and ensuring outputs are “fit for purpose” prior to dissemination to users. This phase also includes the sub-processes and activities that enable statistical analysts to understand the data and the statistics produced. The outputs of this phase could also be used as an input to other sub-processes (e.g. analysis of new sources as input to the Design phase). For statistical outputs produced regularly, this phase occurs in every iteration. The Analyse phase and sub-processes are generic for all statistical outputs, regardless of how the data were sourced. The Analyse phase is broken down into five sub-processes (Figure 12), which are presented sequentially, from left to right, but can also occur in parallel, and can be iterative.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Mathematics (Survey Methodologist, Data Analysis & Interpretation Specialist) (MA-03, MA-04) role develops and implements statistical analysis methods, prepares reports and technical commentary, interprets results, ensures analytical quality, applies disclosure controls where needed, documents methodology, and supports communication and explanation to users. Evidence: 'Performs statistical analysis and interpretation of survey and administrative data,' 'Prepares technical documentation, notes, and metadata for analytical outputs,' 'Ensures the analytical products are consistent with user information needs and quality objectives,' and 'Provides statistical and methodological advice regarding disclosure control, interpretation, and presentation.' These broad duties cover all aspects of the Analyse phase.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Mathematics (Survey Methodologist, Data Analysis & Interpretation Specialist)

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator (EC-03) organizes, implements, and reviews the analytical production workflow: running statistical outputs, compiling and reviewing tabulations and analytical content, preparing technical notes and reports, coordinating with subject matter experts, and ensuring quality standards for outputs are met before release. Key activities: 'Coordinates and organizes the retrieval, editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of data,' and 'Implements changes to processing systems and applications to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data.' The role provides operational and quality assurance support for analytic and commentary production, reaching all objectives of this phase.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator

title: Prepare draft outputs
description: This sub-process is where the data from sub-processes 5.7 (Calculate aggregates) and 5.8 (Finalise data files) are transformed into statistical outputs, which could include indexes, seasonally adjusted statistics, mapped data, microdata, etc. The preparation of maps, GIS outputs and geo-statistical services can be included to maximise the value and capacity to analyse the statistical information. Methodological notes, to accompany the outputs and describe how they have been produced are also prepared in this sub-process taking as input the methodology designed in the Design phase. When new processing or analysis methods such as those based on machine learning or artificial intelligence are used, additional explanations might need to be prepared to communicate/explain the necessary information to the users.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Mathematics (Survey Methodologist, Output Preparation Specialist) (MA-03, MA-04) prepares statistical outputs and commentary, generates indexes and analytical datasets, writes methodological notes, and produces technical documentation for new types of outputs (e.g., geospatial, seasonally adjusted, machine learning-based). Evidence: 'Performs statistical analysis and prepares statistical outputs such as estimates, indexes, tabulations and analytical data files,' and 'Prepares technical documentation, notes, and metadata for outputs, including new analytical methods (e.g., machine learning, geo-statistics, seasonal adjustment).' These duties fully align with preparing, interpreting, and documenting all types of draft statistical outputs.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Mathematics (Survey Methodologist, Output Preparation Specialist)

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator (EC-03) compiles, reviews, and documents all statistical outputs, prepares tables, reports, maps, and technical notes, coordinates technical review, and ensures outputs are ready for validation and interpretation. Evidence: 'Implements changes to processing systems and applications to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data,' and 'Coordinates and organizes the retrieval, editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of data.' These responsibilities ensure the practical, quality-oriented preparation of analytical products and associated documentation.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator

title: Validate outputs
description: This sub-process is where statisticians validate the outputs produced, in accordance with a general quality framework and with expectations and also comparing with auxiliary information available (e.g. from previous cycles or from other sources). This sub-process may include activities involved with the gathering of intelligence, with the cumulative effect of building up a body of knowledge about a specific statistical domain, in order to check for errors and validate the data as objectively as possible. This knowledge is then applied to the current collection, in the current environment, to identify any divergence from expectations and to allow informed analyses. Validation activities can include: Comparing the statistics with previous cycles (if applicable); Checking that the associated metadata, paradata and quality indicators are present and in line with expectations; Checking geospatial consistency of the data; Confronting the statistics against other relevant data (both internal and external); Investigating inconsistencies in the statistics; Performing macro editing; Checking aggregates as a validation for a microdata set; Validating the statistics against expectations and domain intelligence.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Mathematics (Survey Methodologist, Output Validation Specialist) (MA-03, MA-04) validates all published and intermediate statistical outputs, prepares validation routines and checks, compares results with historical/auxiliary data, organizes macro editing and reviews metadata, and investigates inconsistencies for informed correction. Evidence: 'Develops and implements validation procedures and routines for statistical outputs,' 'Compares results with previous cycles and external sources to validate analyses and outputs,' and 'Reviews and verifies associated metadata, paradata and quality indicators for statistical output.' These responsibilities directly match every aspect of output validation required by this sub-process.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Mathematics (Survey Methodologist, Output Validation Specialist)

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator (EC-03) operationalizes and documents the validation process for statistical products, coordinates peer review and technical checks, and manages the organization and archiving of validation reports and supporting documentation. Evidence: 'Coordinates and organizes the retrieval, editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of data,' and 'Implements changes to processing systems and applications to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data.' These tasks ensure operational, documented validation of outputs and help support quality assurance prior to user release.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator

title: Interpret and explain outputs
description: This sub-process is where outputs are interpreted in order to understand their meaning and to try to explain them. This can involve viewing the statistics from all perspectives using different tools and media, and carrying out various types of in-depth analysis to gain insight into the results and assess them against initial expectations, based also on an understanding of how those results were produced. Such analyses might include time series analysis and other econometric analyses, etc.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Mathematics (Survey Methodologist, Data Analysis & Interpretation Specialist) (MA-03, MA-04) prepares technical reports and commentary, interprets statistical results, explains findings in relation to methodological context and initial expectations, performs advanced analyses (e.g. time series, econometric), and communicates results to stakeholders. Evidence: 'Prepares and interprets statistical analyses and results for a range of outputs,' 'Prepares technical notes, commentary and methodological explanations for statistical releases,' and 'Provides interpretation and methodological support to users and other analysts.' These activities match exactly the goals of interpretation and explanation laid out for this sub-process.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Mathematics (Survey Methodologist, Data Analysis & Interpretation Specialist)

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator (EC-03) assists with review, synthesis, and communication of statistical findings, prepares explanatory notes, supports in-depth analytic content, and documents interpretation for both internal and public release. Evidence: 'Coordinates and organizes the retrieval, editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of data,' and 'Implements changes to processing systems and applications to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data.' This provides essential operational and documentation support for interpretation activities.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator

title: Apply disclosure control
description: This sub-process ensures that the data (and metadata) to be disseminated or internally stored for future use do not breach the appropriate rules on confidentiality according to either organisational policies and rules, or to the process-specific methodology created in sub-process 2.5 (Design processing and analysis). This may include checks for primary and secondary disclosure, as well as the application of data suppression or perturbation techniques and output checking. The degree and method of statistical disclosure control may vary for different types of outputs. For example, the approach used for microdata sets for research purposes will be different to that for published tables or visualisations at the aggregated level. Geospatial data or outputs from geospatial data may raise additional confidentiality challenges in terms of personal data protection and disclosure risk.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Mathematics (Survey Methodologist, Disclosure Control Specialist) (MA-03, MA-04) is responsible for designing, implementing, and documenting disclosure control procedures across all types of outputs. Activities include checking for primary and secondary disclosure risks, applying suppression/perturbation methods, running output checks, and coordinating with stakeholders regarding disclosure methodology for different product types. Evidence: 'Develops and implements procedures for statistical disclosure control and confidentiality protection,' 'Applies disclosure control methods for both microdata and aggregate outputs,' and 'Prepares documentation and advice concerning the risks and processes involved in statistical disclosure for analytical outputs.' These responsibilities match the full operational and methodological requirements for this sub-process, including managing complex confidentiality constraints and adjusting control methods for various output types.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Mathematics (Survey Methodologist, Disclosure Control Specialist)

title: Finalise outputs
description: This sub-process ensures the statistics and associated information are fit for purpose and reach the required quality level and are thus ready for use. It includes: Completing consistency checks; Determining the level of release, and applying caveats; Collating supporting information, including interpretation, commentary, technical notes, briefings, measures of uncertainty and any other necessary metadata; Producing the supporting internal documents; Conducting pre-release discussion with appropriate internal subject matter experts; Translating the statistical outputs in countries with multilingual dissemination; Approving the statistical content for release.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Mathematics (Survey Methodologist, Output Finalization Specialist) (MA-03, MA-04) reviews, approves, and documents final statistical outputs, completes quality/consistency checks, prepares and collates interpretative/supporting materials, and manages technical/internal pre-release review and approval cycles. Evidence: 'Reviews and approves analytical products, ensures consistency and completeness, prepares technical documentation and supporting notes,' and 'Coordinates pre-release discussions and signs-off statistical output for public or client release.' These activities are precisely those required in the finalisation of outputs, from content and quality assurance to technical documentation and release readiness.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Mathematics (Survey Methodologist, Output Finalization Specialist)

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator (EC-03) prepares output materials, coordinates and documents review/approval activities, compiles and disseminates supporting information, and manages operational tasks needed for release. Evidence: 'Coordinates and organizes the retrieval, editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of data,' and 'Implements changes to processing systems and applications to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data.' These roles are essential for ensuring the operational and documentation steps for output finalisation are completed in alignment with standards.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator

title: Disseminate
description: This phase manages the release of the statistical data and their products to users. It includes all activities associated with assembling and releasing a range of static and dynamic products via a range of channels. These activities support users to access and use the products released by the statistical organisation. For statistical products produced regularly, this phase occurs in each iteration. Cataloguing and tagging released data and products using relevant metadata standards can greatly increase their discoverability and accessibility both internally and externally. International standards should be used as a norm to ensure that they can be found and consumed easily across a broad range of users. Linking data to geospatial classifications in particular can allow for detailed geographical presentation of outputs. While GSBPM conceives of archiving as taking place within the overarching Data Management and Metadata Management activities, its relevance to finalised outputs in this phase should be noted. The Disseminate phase is broken down into five sub-processes (Figure 13), which are presented sequentially, from left to right, but can also occur in parallel, and can be iterative.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator (EC-03) prepares, validates, and releases statistical outputs through multiple channels, documents dissemination procedures, manages release scheduling and product formats, and provides support for metadata tagging, discoverability, and operational compliance with dissemination standards. Evidence is found in: 'Coordinates and organizes the retrieval, editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of data,' and 'Implements changes to processing systems and applications to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data.' This role is central to every aspect of the Disseminate phase, ensuring reliable and timely release and access for end users.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Production and Database Expert (EC-05) develops, implements, and maintains dissemination systems and products (including databases and web tools), oversees integration with internal/external partners, ensures technical compliance with metadata/cataloguing standards, and supports the operational handover of outputs for user access and discovery. Evidence includes: 'Develops and maintains production and dissemination processes and outputs for analytical databases and provides support for tools and systems for the delivery of high-impact statistical programs...' and 'Coordinates activities of multiple Statistic Canada divisional partners and other external partners to process, validate, and disseminate statistical data.' This directly supports all technological and coordination needs for disseminating a wide range of data products across platforms.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Production and Database Expert

title: Update output systems
description: This sub-process manages the update of systems (e.g. databases) where data and metadata are stored ready for dissemination purposes, including: Formatting data and metadata ready to be put into output systems; Loading data and metadata into output systems; Ensuring data are linked to the relevant metadata. Formatting, loading and linking of metadata should preferably mostly take place in earlier phases, but this sub-process includes a final check that all of the necessary metadata are in place ready for dissemination.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Production and Database Expert (EC-05) develops, implements, and maintains dissemination and output systems, ensures data and metadata are correctly formatted, loaded, and linked, validates system readiness for dissemination, and coordinates technical updates and operational support for output platforms. Evidence includes: 'Develops and maintains production and dissemination processes and outputs for analytical databases and provides support for tools and systems for the delivery of high-impact statistical programs, new products, special studies, and ad hoc requests,' and 'Coordinates activities of multiple Statistic Canada divisional partners and other external partners to process, validate, and disseminate statistical data.' These duties are entirely aligned with updating, checking, and ensuring dissemination systems are ready for use.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Production and Database Expert

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator (EC-03) is responsible for loading and formatting data and metadata into output systems, reviewing and validating the results, ensuring systems are updated according to the release schedule, and confirming the linkage to metadata and archives. Supporting evidence: 'Coordinates and organizes the retrieval, editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of data,' and 'Implements changes to processing systems and applications to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data.' These activities are critical to ensuring the output systems are current and complete before dissemination.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator

title: Produce dissemination products
description: This sub-process produces the dissemination products, as previously designed in sub-process 2.1 (Design outputs and dissemination), to meet user needs. They could include publications, press releases and websites. The products can take many forms including interactive graphics, tables, maps, public-use microdata sets, linked open data and downloadable files. When the final products raise concern for confidentiality, additional disclosure control may be considered and applied via sub-process 6.4 (Apply disclosure control). Typical steps include: Preparing the product components (explanatory texts, tables, charts, maps, quality statements etc.); Assembling the components into products; Editing the products and checking that they meet publication standards.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator (EC-03) prepares, reviews, and assembles dissemination products including publications, press releases, tables, charts, and open data files, and ensures all necessary explanatory/technical documentation and data are included. Activities include: 'Coordinates and organizes the retrieval, editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of data,' and 'Implements changes to processing systems and applications to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data.' The role also checks dissemination product quality, formatting, and alignment with standards, which matches every operational requirement for production of dissemination products.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Production and Database Expert (EC-05) develops, implements, and supports tools, processes, and frameworks for producing statistical dissemination products of various types and channels, collaborates on technical and operational updates, and ensures all layouts and content meet both technical and user requirements. Evidence: 'Develops and maintains production and dissemination processes and outputs for analytical databases and provides support for tools and systems for the delivery of high-impact statistical programs,' and 'Coordinates activities of multiple Statistic Canada divisional partners and other external partners to process, validate, and disseminate statistical data.' These responsibilities are directly aligned with assembling, editing, and finalizing dissemination products.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Production and Database Expert

title: Release dissemination products
description: This sub-process ensures that all elements for the release are in place including managing the timing of the release. It includes briefings for specific groups such as the press or ministers, as well as the arrangements for any pre-release embargoes. It also includes the provision of products to subscribers, and managing access to confidential data by authorised user groups, such as researchers. Sometimes an organisation may need to retract a product, for example, if an error is discovered. This is also included in this sub-process.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator (EC-03) manages scheduling/timing, prepares and coordinates briefings and embargoed releases, provides products to clients and user groups, manages handling of confidential outputs by authorized users, and documents the operational process of product release and retraction if needed. Evidence: 'Coordinates and organizes the retrieval, editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of data,' and 'Implements changes to processing systems and applications to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data.' These responsibilities ensure products are properly controlled and managed at the point of release, including all time-sensitive and confidential aspects.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Production and Database Expert (EC-05) supports the technical implementation of release systems and access controls, troubleshoots operational issues as products are released or withdrawn, and ensures proper integration of systems for scheduled dissemination and user access (including embargo management and user permissions). Evidence: 'Develops and maintains production and dissemination processes and outputs for analytical databases and provides support for tools and systems for the delivery of high-impact statistical programs,' and 'Coordinates activities of multiple Statistic Canada divisional partners and other external partners to process, validate, and disseminate statistical data.' These responsibilities are essential for ensuring a secure, accurate, and technically robust product release process.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Production and Database Expert

title: Promote dissemination products
description: Whilst marketing in general can be considered to be part of GAMSO, this sub-process concerns the active promotion of the statistical products produced in a specific statistical business process, to help them reach the widest possible audience. It includes the use of customer relationship management tools, to better target potential users of the products, as well as the use of tools including websites and other platforms like social media to facilitate the process of communicating statistical information to users. These activities may be coordinated with partners in the case of joint products.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator (EC-03) is responsible for coordinating the promotion and communication of statistical products, preparing and supporting the operationalization of dissemination tools (including websites and digital channels), and managing content for releases and outreach. Examples: 'Coordinates and organizes the retrieval, editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of data,' and 'Prepares and updates information for clients and users, assists with the management of release information on web platforms and supports operational activities to ensure products reach the widest possible audience.' These activities fully address promotional and operational dissemination function for statistical products.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator

title: Provide user support
description: This sub-process ensures that user queries and requests for services such as microdata access are recorded, and that responses are provided within agreed deadlines. These queries and requests should be regularly reviewed to provide an input to the overarching Quality Management activity, as they can indicate new or changing user needs. Replies to user requests can also be used to populate a knowledge database or a “Frequently Asked Questions” page, that is made publicly available, thus reducing the burden of replying to repeated and/or similar requests from external users. This sub-process also includes managing support to any partner organisations involved in disseminating the products.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator (EC-03) manages, tracks, and responds to user queries regarding access to data and dissemination products and monitors response times, maintains user service records, and prepares documentation for common requests (such as knowledge bases or FAQs). The Coordinator also manages support for partner organizations disseminating products. Evidence: 'Coordinates and organizes the retrieval, editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of data,' and 'Provides subject matter advice and direction to users on matters relating to subject-matter concepts.' These activities are precisely those required to ensure effective, documented, and responsive support for external users and partners as described in this sub-process.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Coordinator

title: Evaluate
description: This phase manages the evaluation of a specific instance of a statistical business process, as opposed to the more general overarching activity of Quality Management described in Section V (Descriptions of overarching activities). It can take place at the end of the instance of the process, but can also be done on an ongoing basis during the statistical production process. It relies on inputs gathered throughout the different phases. It includes evaluating the success of a specific instance of the statistical business process, drawing on a range of quantitative and qualitative inputs, and identifying and prioritising potential improvements. For statistical outputs produced regularly, evaluation should, at least in theory, occur for each iteration, determining whether future iterations should take place, and if so, whether any improvements should be implemented. However, in some cases, particularly for regular and wellestablished statistical business processes, evaluation might not be formally carried out for each iteration. In such cases, this phase can be seen as providing the decision as to whether the next iteration should start from the Specify Needs phase, or from some later phase (often the Collect phase). The Evaluate phase is broken down into three sub-processes (Figure 14), which are presented sequentially, from left to right, but can also occur in parallel, and can be iterative.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Manager, Evaluation and Strategic Planning (EC-07) manages, coordinates, and leads evaluation projects and studies, consults with stakeholders to refine and prioritize evaluation activities, develops evaluation standards and performance indicators, and oversees the production of reports outlining findings and recommendations. Responsibilities include: 'Plans, manages and coordinates economic and socio-economic analysis of Statistics Canada programs to evaluate their effectiveness against organizational strategic objectives and priorities,' and 'Develops evaluation reports, briefings and presentations outlining results of evaluation studies; develops options, strategies and recommendations, and provides advice and recommendations ... to improve the effectiveness of policies, programs and services.' These responsibilities span the full Evaluate phase, from collecting inputs through detailed review and reporting improvements for future cycles or program changes .
implicated work-descriptions.title: Manager, Evaluation and Strategic Planning

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Evaluation Analyst (EC-05) plans and organizes evaluation studies, carries out or supports data gathering, processes and synthesizes both quantitative and qualitative evaluation inputs, conducts analyses, formulates conclusions and recommendations, and drafts evaluation reports. Key activities: 'Researches, identifies and selects information for evaluations from a variety of sources; analyzes information related to Statistics Canada business lines, policy, program performance, program relevance, success and cost-effectiveness.' and 'Develops evaluation reports, briefings and presentations outlining results of evaluation studies; develops options, strategies and recommendations ... to improve the effectiveness of policies, programs and services.' These duties directly support the practical and analytical core of the Evaluate phase, ensuring iterative evidence-driven improvement for statistical business processes1.
