implicated work-descriptions.title: Evaluation Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Evaluation Officer (EC-03) participates in project teams for evaluation studies, conducts research and data collection, analyzes and synthesizes evaluation data, prepares recommendations, contributes to reporting, and attends meetings to discuss findings and recommend improvements. Activities: 'Participates as a member of project teams, in the conduct of evaluation studies related to Statistics Canada programs, policies and initiatives, to evaluate their relevance and performance, under the supervision of the Evaluation Manager.' and 'Assesses current requirements for data; interprets and analyzes information and databases to support findings and conclusions concerning various elements of Statistics Canada evaluations.' This role performs hands-on technical work supporting the evaluation process, information collection, and performance review2.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Evaluation Officer

title: Gather evaluation inputs
description: Evaluation material can be produced in any other phase or sub-process. It may take many forms, including feedback from users, process metadata (paradata), system metrics, and staff suggestions. Reports of progress against an action plan agreed during a previous iteration may also form an input to evaluations of subsequent iterations. This sub-process gathers all of these inputs, compiles quality indicators and makes them available for the person or team producing the evaluation. The collection of some of these evaluation materials can be automated and take place in a continuous way throughout the whole process, as defined by the quality framework (see Quality Management in Section V). On the other hand, for the evaluation of certain processes it can be necessary to perform specific activities such as small surveys, (e.g. post-enumeration surveys, re-interview studies, survey on effectiveness of dissemination).

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Evaluation Analyst (EC-05) gathers, reviews, and synthesizes evaluation inputs from a range of sources (e.g., user feedback, process data, system metrics, post-activity surveys, and performance indicators), organizes findings, and documents evaluation material for subsequent analysis. This role is explicitly responsible for the review and collection of quality and process indicators, input from previous cycles, and evidence from specific studies or surveys. Evidence: 'Researches, identifies and selects information for evaluations from a variety of sources; analyzes information related to Statistics Canada business lines, policy, program performance, program relevance, success and cost-effectiveness.' This aligns perfectly with the requirements for gathering evaluation inputs in this sub-process.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Evaluation Analyst

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Evaluation Officer (EC-03) collects feedback and process data, conducts interviews and surveys, attends meetings to discuss evaluation requirements, and organizes the data for use by the evaluation team or manager. Key activities: 'Participates as a member of project teams, in the conduct of evaluation studies related to Statistics Canada programs, policies and initiatives, to evaluate their relevance and performance, under the supervision of the Evaluation Manager,' and 'Attends departmental and inter-departmental meetings, when required, to discuss files, issues and evaluation requirements; interprets and reports on trends...' The Officer's focus on hands-on data gathering and information organization is the essence of this sub-process.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Evaluation Officer

title: Conduct evaluation
description: This sub-process analyses the evaluation inputs, compares them to the expected/target benchmarking results (when available), and synthesises them into an evaluation report or control dashboard. The evaluation can take place at the end of the whole process (ex-post evaluation), for selected activities, during its execution in a continuous way, or throughout the process, thus allowing for quick fixes or continuous improvement. The resulting report should note any quality issues specific to this iteration of the statistical business process as well as highlighting any deviation of performance metrics from expected values, and should make recommendations for changes if appropriate. These recommendations can cover changes to any phase or sub-process for future iterations of the process, or can suggest that the process is not repeated.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Manager, Evaluation and Strategic Planning (EC-07) leads, synthesizes, and oversees the analysis of evaluation inputs, produces high-level reports, identifies quality issues, recommends improvements, and communicates results across the statistical organization. Key evidence: 'Plans, manages and coordinates economic and socio-economic analysis of Statistics Canada programs to evaluate their effectiveness against organizational strategic objectives and priorities.' and 'Develops evaluation reports, briefings and presentations outlining results of evaluation studies; develops options, strategies and recommendations, and provides advice and recommendations ... to improve the effectiveness of policies, programs and services.' These functions are direct matches for the conduct and synthesis of evaluation and reporting required in this sub-process.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Manager, Evaluation and Strategic Planning

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Evaluation Analyst (EC-05) analyzes, interprets, and synthesizes gathered evaluation data, compares performance indicators to targets, drafts evaluation reports, and devises quality improvement recommendations. Relevant activities include: 'Researches, identifies and selects information for evaluations from a variety of sources; analyzes information related to Statistics Canada business lines, policy, program performance, program relevance, success and cost-effectiveness.' and 'Develops evaluation reports, briefings and presentations outlining results of evaluation studies; develops options, strategies and recommendations to improve the effectiveness of policies, programs and services.' This is directly aligned to the required activities in synthesizing and reporting on the evaluation.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Evaluation Analyst

title: Agree an action plan
description: This sub-process brings together the necessary decision-making power to form and agree an action plan based on the evaluation report. It should also include consideration of a mechanism for monitoring the impact of those actions, which may, in turn, provide an input to evaluations of future iterations of the process.

implicated work-descriptions.justification: The Manager, Evaluation and Strategic Planning (EC-07) is responsible for facilitating consensus among management and stakeholders on recommendations, formalizing and communicating the agreed action plan, leading the development of mechanisms for tracking progress, and ensuring that results and decisions are circulated to guide future evaluation and iteration. Evidence: 'Develops evaluation reports, briefings and presentations outlining results of evaluation studies; develops options, strategies and recommendations, and provides advice and recommendations ... to improve the effectiveness of policies, programs and services.' and 'Formulates, coordinates and communicates new policies, standards, frameworks and procedures and monitors their implementation to ensure quality.' These activities perfectly match the requirements for coordinating, documenting, and monitoring action plan implementation after evaluation.
implicated work-descriptions.title: Manager, Evaluation and Strategic Planning
